Artificial rivers (canals) and ponds are a part of Azerbaijan's water systems. In terms of water supply, Azerbaijan is below the average in the world with approximately 100,000 cubic metres (3,531,467 cubic feet) per year of water per square kilometer.<sup id="cite_ref-KL_141-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-KL-141">&#91;138&#93;</a></sup> All big <a href="/wiki/Reservoir" title="Reservoir">water reservoirs</a> are built on Kur. The hydrography of Azerbaijan basically belongs to the <a href="/wiki/Caspian_Sea_basin" class="mw-redirect" title="Caspian Sea basin">Caspian Sea basin</a>.
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Kura_(Caspian_Sea)" class="mw-redirect" title="Kura (Caspian Sea)">Kura</a> and <a href="/wiki/Aras_River" class="mw-redirect" title="Aras River">Aras</a> are the major rivers in Azerbaijan. They run through the <a href="/wiki/Kura-Aras_Lowland" class="mw-redirect" title="Kura-Aras Lowland">Kura-Aras Lowland</a>. The rivers that directly flow into the Caspian Sea, originate mainly from the north-eastern slope of the Major Caucasus and <a href="/wiki/Talysh_Mountains" title="Talysh Mountains">Talysh Mountains</a> and run along the Samur–Devechi and Lankaran lowlands.<sup id="cite_ref-142" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-142">&#91;139&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Yanar_Dag" class="mw-redirect" title="Yanar Dag">Yanar Dag</a>, translated as "burning mountain", is a natural gas fire which blazes continuously on a hillside on the <a href="/wiki/Absheron_Peninsula" title="Absheron Peninsula">Absheron Peninsula</a> on the <a href="/wiki/Caspian_Sea" title="Caspian Sea">Caspian Sea</a> near <a href="/wiki/Baku" title="Baku">Baku</a>, which itself is known as the "land of fire." Flames jet out into the air from a thin, porous sandstone layer. It is a tourist attraction to visitors to the Baku area.<sup id="cite_ref-143" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-143">&#91;140&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Biodiversity">Biodiversity</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Wildlife_of_Azerbaijan" title="Wildlife of Azerbaijan">Wildlife of Azerbaijan</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/Fauna_of_Azerbaijan" title="Fauna of Azerbaijan">Fauna of Azerbaijan</a> and <a href="/wiki/Flora_of_Azerbaijan" title="Flora of Azerbaijan">Flora of Azerbaijan</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Stamps_of_Azerbaijan,_2006-750.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fd/Stamps_of_Azerbaijan%2C_2006-750.jpg/220px-Stamps_of_Azerbaijan%2C_2006-750.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="159" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fd/Stamps_of_Azerbaijan%2C_2006-750.jpg/330px-Stamps_of_Azerbaijan%2C_2006-750.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fd/Stamps_of_Azerbaijan%2C_2006-750.jpg/440px-Stamps_of_Azerbaijan%2C_2006-750.jpg 2x" data-file-width="614" data-file-height="445" /></a><figcaption>The <a href="/wiki/Karabakh_horse" title="Karabakh horse">Karabakh horse</a> is the national animal of Azerbaijan.</figcaption></figure>
<p>The first reports on the richness and diversity of animal life in Azerbaijan can be found in travel notes of Eastern travelers. Animal carvings on architectural monuments, ancient rocks, and stones survived up to the present times. The first information on flora and fauna of Azerbaijan was collected during the visits of naturalists to Azerbaijan in the 17th century.<sup id="cite_ref-GEO_135-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-GEO-135">&#91;132&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>There are 106 species of mammals, 97 species of fish, 363 species of birds, 10 species of amphibians, and 52 species of reptiles which have been recorded and classified in Azerbaijan.<sup id="cite_ref-GEO_135-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-GEO-135">&#91;132&#93;</a></sup> The national animal of Azerbaijan is the <a href="/wiki/Karabakh_horse" title="Karabakh horse">Karabakh horse</a>, a mountain-steppe racing and riding horse endemic to Azerbaijan. The Karabakh horse has a reputation for its good temper, speed, elegance, and intelligence. It is one of the oldest breeds, with ancestry dating to the ancient world, but today the horse is an endangered species.<sup id="cite_ref-144" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-144">&#91;141&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Azerbaijan's flora consists of more than 4,500 species of <a href="/wiki/Higher_plants" class="mw-redirect" title="Higher plants">higher plants</a>. Due to the unique climate in Azerbaijan, the flora is much richer in the number of species than the flora of the other republics of the South Caucasus. 66 percent of the species growing in the whole <a href="/wiki/Caucasus" title="Caucasus">Caucasus</a> can be found in Azerbaijan.<sup id="cite_ref-145" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-145">&#91;142&#93;</a></sup> The country lies within four ecoregions: <a href="/wiki/Caspian_Hyrcanian_mixed_forests" class="mw-redirect" title="Caspian Hyrcanian mixed forests">Caspian Hyrcanian mixed forests</a>, <a href="/wiki/Caucasus_mixed_forests" title="Caucasus mixed forests">Caucasus mixed forests</a>, <a href="/wiki/Eastern_Anatolian_montane_steppe" title="Eastern Anatolian montane steppe">Eastern Anatolian montane steppe</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijan_shrub_desert_and_steppe" title="Azerbaijan shrub desert and steppe">Azerbaijan shrub desert and steppe</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-DinersteinOlson2017_146-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-DinersteinOlson2017-146">&#91;143&#93;</a></sup> Azerbaijan had a 2018 <a href="/wiki/Forest_Landscape_Integrity_Index" title="Forest Landscape Integrity Index">Forest Landscape Integrity Index</a> mean score of 6.55/10, ranking it 72nd globally out of 172 countries.<sup id="cite_ref-FLII-Supplementary_147-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FLII-Supplementary-147">&#91;144&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Government_and_politics">Government and politics</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Politics_of_Azerbaijan" title="Politics of Azerbaijan">Politics of Azerbaijan</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Elections_in_Azerbaijan" title="Elections in Azerbaijan">Elections in Azerbaijan</a> and <a href="/wiki/Human_rights_in_Azerbaijan" title="Human rights in Azerbaijan">Human rights in Azerbaijan</a></div>
<figure class="mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Gobierno_de_Azerbaiy%C3%A1n,_Baku,_Azerbaiy%C3%A1n,_2016-09-26,_DD_27.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/e/ec/Gobierno_de_Azerbaiy%C3%A1n%2C_Baku%2C_Azerbaiy%C3%A1n%2C_2016-09-26%2C_DD_27.jpg/280px-Gobierno_de_Azerbaiy%C3%A1n%2C_Baku%2C_Azerbaiy%C3%A1n%2C_2016-09-26%2C_DD_27.jpg" decoding="async" width="280" height="143" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/e/ec/Gobierno_de_Azerbaiy%C3%A1n%2C_Baku%2C_Azerbaiy%C3%A1n%2C_2016-09-26%2C_DD_27.jpg/420px-Gobierno_de_Azerbaiy%C3%A1n%2C_Baku%2C_Azerbaiy%C3%A1n%2C_2016-09-26%2C_DD_27.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/e/ec/Gobierno_de_Azerbaiy%C3%A1n%2C_Baku%2C_Azerbaiy%C3%A1n%2C_2016-09-26%2C_DD_27.jpg/560px-Gobierno_de_Azerbaiy%C3%A1n%2C_Baku%2C_Azerbaiy%C3%A1n%2C_2016-09-26%2C_DD_27.jpg 2x" data-file-width="8083" data-file-height="4132" /></a><figcaption>Government building in Baku</figcaption></figure>
<p>Azerbaijan's government functions as an <a href="/wiki/Authoritarian" class="mw-redirect" title="Authoritarian">authoritarian</a> regime in practice;<sup id="cite_ref-148" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-148">&#91;145&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-149" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-149">&#91;146&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-150" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-150">&#91;147&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-151" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-151">&#91;148&#93;</a></sup> although it regularly holds <a href="/wiki/Elections_in_Azerbaijan" title="Elections in Azerbaijan">elections</a>, these are marred by <a href="/wiki/Electoral_fraud" title="Electoral fraud">electoral fraud</a> and other unfair election practices.<sup id="cite_ref-152" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-152">&#91;149&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-153" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-153">&#91;150&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-154" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-154">&#91;151&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-155" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-155">&#91;152&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-156" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-156">&#91;153&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-157" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-157">&#91;154&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-158" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-158">&#91;155&#93;</a></sup> Azerbaijan has been ruled by the <a href="/wiki/Political_family#Other_countries" title="Political family">Aliyev political family</a> and the <a href="/wiki/New_Azerbaijan_Party" title="New Azerbaijan Party">New Azerbaijan Party</a> (<i>Yeni Azərbaycan Partiyası</i>, YAP) established by <a href="/wiki/Heydar_Aliyev" title="Heydar Aliyev">Heydar Aliyev</a> continuously since 1993.<sup id="cite_ref-159" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-159">&#91;156&#93;</a></sup> It is categorised as "not free" by <a href="/wiki/Freedom_House" title="Freedom House">Freedom House</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-Freedom_House_160-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Freedom_House-160">&#91;157&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-frh_161-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-frh-161">&#91;158&#93;</a></sup> who ranked it 9/100 on Global Freedom Score in 2022, calling it a "consolidated authoritarian regime".<sup id="cite_ref-162" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-162">&#91;159&#93;</a></sup> 
</p><p>The structural formation of Azerbaijan's political system was completed by the adoption of the new <a href="/wiki/Constitution_of_Azerbaijan" title="Constitution of Azerbaijan">Constitution</a> on 12 November 1995. According to Article 23 of the Constitution, the <a href="/wiki/National_symbol" title="National symbol">state symbols</a> of the Azerbaijan Republic are the <a href="/wiki/Flag_of_Azerbaijan" title="Flag of Azerbaijan">flag</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Coat_of_arms_of_Azerbaijan" class="mw-redirect" title="Coat of arms of Azerbaijan">coat of arms</a>, and the <a href="/wiki/National_Anthem_of_the_Republic_of_Azerbaijan" class="mw-redirect" title="National Anthem of the Republic of Azerbaijan">national anthem</a>. The state power in Azerbaijan is limited only by law for internal issues, but international affairs are also limited by international agreements' provisions.<sup id="cite_ref-163" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-163">&#91;160&#93;</a></sup><sup class="noprint Inline-Template noprint noexcerpt Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:NOTRS" class="mw-redirect" title="Wikipedia:NOTRS"><span title="This claim needs references to better sources. (September 2023)">better&#160;source&#160;needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup>
</p><p>The Constitution of Azerbaijan states that it is a presidential republic with three branches of power – Executive, Legislative, and Judicial. The legislative power is held by the <a href="/wiki/Unicameralism" title="Unicameralism">unicameral</a> <a href="/wiki/National_Assembly_of_Azerbaijan" class="mw-redirect" title="National Assembly of Azerbaijan">National Assembly</a> and the Supreme National Assembly in the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic. The Parliament of Azerbaijan, called Milli Majlis, consists of 125 deputies elected based on <a href="/wiki/First_past_the_post" class="mw-redirect" title="First past the post">majority vote</a>, with a term of five years for each elected member. The elections are held every five years, on the first Sunday of November. The Parliament is not responsible for the formation of the government, but the Constitution requires the approval of the Cabinet of Ministers by Milli Majlis.<sup id="cite_ref-164" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-164">&#91;161&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/New_Azerbaijan_Party" title="New Azerbaijan Party">New Azerbaijan Party</a>, and independents loyal to the ruling government, currently hold almost all of the Parliament's 125 seats. During the <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijani_parliamentary_election,_2010" class="mw-redirect" title="Azerbaijani parliamentary election, 2010">2010 Parliamentary election</a>, the opposition parties, <a href="/wiki/Musavat" title="Musavat">Musavat</a> and <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijani_Popular_Front_Party" title="Azerbaijani Popular Front Party">Azerbaijani Popular Front Party</a>, failed to win a single seat. European observers <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijani_parliamentary_election,_2010#Campaign_irregularities" class="mw-redirect" title="Azerbaijani parliamentary election, 2010">found numerous irregularities</a> in the run-up to the election and <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijani_parliamentary_election,_2010#Election" class="mw-redirect" title="Azerbaijani parliamentary election, 2010">on election day</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-165" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-165">&#91;162&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Munich_Security_Conference_2010_-_Ilham_Aliyev.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f8/Munich_Security_Conference_2010_-_Ilham_Aliyev.jpg/170px-Munich_Security_Conference_2010_-_Ilham_Aliyev.jpg" decoding="async" width="170" height="255" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f8/Munich_Security_Conference_2010_-_Ilham_Aliyev.jpg/255px-Munich_Security_Conference_2010_-_Ilham_Aliyev.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f8/Munich_Security_Conference_2010_-_Ilham_Aliyev.jpg/340px-Munich_Security_Conference_2010_-_Ilham_Aliyev.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2336" data-file-height="3504" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Ilham_Aliyev" title="Ilham Aliyev">Ilham Aliyev</a>, Azerbaijan's fourth and current President, succeeded his father <a href="/wiki/Heydar_Aliyev" title="Heydar Aliyev">Heydar Aliyev</a> in 2003.</figcaption></figure>
<p>The executive power is held by the <a href="/wiki/President_of_Azerbaijan" title="President of Azerbaijan">President</a>, who is elected for a seven-year term by direct elections, and the <a href="/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Azerbaijan" title="Prime Minister of Azerbaijan">Prime Minister</a>. The president is authorized to form the <a href="/wiki/Cabinet_of_Azerbaijan" title="Cabinet of Azerbaijan">Cabinet</a>, a collective executive body accountable to both the President and the National Assembly.<sup id="cite_ref-LaPorte2016_8-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-LaPorte2016-8">&#91;6&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Cabinet_of_Azerbaijan" title="Cabinet of Azerbaijan">Cabinet of Azerbaijan</a> consists primarily of the prime minister, his deputies, and ministers. The <a href="/wiki/8th_Government_of_Azerbaijan" title="8th Government of Azerbaijan">8th Government of Azerbaijan</a> is the administration in its current formation. The president does not have the right to dissolve the National Assembly but has the right to veto its decisions. To override the presidential veto, the parliament must have a majority of 95 votes. The judicial power is vested in the <a href="/wiki/Constitutional_Court_of_Azerbaijan" title="Constitutional Court of Azerbaijan">Constitutional Court</a>, <a href="/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_Azerbaijan" title="Supreme Court of Azerbaijan">Supreme Court</a>, and the Economic Court. The president nominates the judges in these courts.<sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (September 2023)">citation needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup>
</p><p>Azerbaijan's system of governance nominally can be called two-tiered. The top or highest tier of the government is the Executive Power headed by President. The President appoints the Cabinet of Ministers and other high-ranking officials. The Local Executive Authority is merely a continuation of Executive Power. The Provision determines the legal status of local state administration in Azerbaijan on Local Executive Authority (<i>Yerli Icra Hakimiyati</i>), adopted 16 June 1999. In June 2012, the President approved the new Regulation, which granted additional powers to Local Executive Authorities, strengthening their dominant position in Azerbaijan's local affairs<sup id="cite_ref-166" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-166">&#91;163&#93;</a></sup> The Security Council is the deliberative body under the president, and he organizes it according to the Constitution. It was established on 10 April 1997. The administrative department is not a part of the president's office but manages the financial, technical and pecuniary activities of both the president and his office.<sup id="cite_ref-167" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-167">&#91;164&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Foreign_relations">Foreign relations</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Foreign_relations_of_Azerbaijan" title="Foreign relations of Azerbaijan">Foreign relations of Azerbaijan</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijan_and_the_European_Union" class="mw-redirect" title="Azerbaijan and the European Union">Azerbaijan and the European Union</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:%C4%B0lham_%C6%8Fliyev%C9%99_T%C3%BCrk_D%C3%BCnyas%C4%B1n%C4%B1n_Ali_Ordeni_t%C9%99qdim_edilib_(2).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/20/%C4%B0lham_%C6%8Fliyev%C9%99_T%C3%BCrk_D%C3%BCnyas%C4%B1n%C4%B1n_Ali_Ordeni_t%C9%99qdim_edilib_%282%29.jpg/220px-%C4%B0lham_%C6%8Fliyev%C9%99_T%C3%BCrk_D%C3%BCnyas%C4%B1n%C4%B1n_Ali_Ordeni_t%C9%99qdim_edilib_%282%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="164" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/20/%C4%B0lham_%C6%8Fliyev%C9%99_T%C3%BCrk_D%C3%BCnyas%C4%B1n%C4%B1n_Ali_Ordeni_t%C9%99qdim_edilib_%282%29.jpg/330px-%C4%B0lham_%C6%8Fliyev%C9%99_T%C3%BCrk_D%C3%BCnyas%C4%B1n%C4%B1n_Ali_Ordeni_t%C9%99qdim_edilib_%282%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/20/%C4%B0lham_%C6%8Fliyev%C9%99_T%C3%BCrk_D%C3%BCnyas%C4%B1n%C4%B1n_Ali_Ordeni_t%C9%99qdim_edilib_%282%29.jpg/440px-%C4%B0lham_%C6%8Fliyev%C9%99_T%C3%BCrk_D%C3%BCnyas%C4%B1n%C4%B1n_Ali_Ordeni_t%C9%99qdim_edilib_%282%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1737" data-file-height="1292" /></a><figcaption>President <a href="/wiki/%C4%B0lham_Aliyev" class="mw-redirect" title="İlham Aliyev">İlham Aliyev</a> receiving the Supreme Order of the Turkic World from Turkish President <a href="/wiki/Recep_Tayyip_Erdo%C4%9Fan" title="Recep Tayyip Erdoğan">Recep Tayyip Erdoğan</a> during the 8th summit of the <a href="/wiki/Organization_of_Turkic_States" title="Organization of Turkic States">Organization of Turkic States</a> in <a href="/wiki/Istanbul" title="Istanbul">Istanbul</a>, <a href="/wiki/Turkey" title="Turkey">Turkey</a>, November 12, 2021</figcaption></figure>
<p>The short-lived Azerbaijan Democratic Republic succeeded in establishing diplomatic relations with six countries, sending diplomatic representatives to Germany and Finland.<sup id="cite_ref-CSUS_168-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-CSUS-168">&#91;165&#93;</a></sup> The process of international recognition of Azerbaijan's independence from the collapsing Soviet Union lasted roughly one year. The most recent country to recognize Azerbaijan was Bahrain, on 6 November 1996.<sup id="cite_ref-169" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-169">&#91;166&#93;</a></sup> Full diplomatic relations, including mutual exchanges of missions, were first established with Turkey, Pakistan, the United States, Iran<sup id="cite_ref-CSUS_168-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-CSUS-168">&#91;165&#93;</a></sup> and Israel.<sup id="cite_ref-israelmfa_170-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-israelmfa-170">&#91;167&#93;</a></sup> Azerbaijan has placed a particular emphasis on its "<a href="/wiki/Special_relationship_(international_relations)" title="Special relationship (international relations)">special relationship</a>" with <a href="/wiki/Turkey" title="Turkey">Turkey</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-171" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-171">&#91;168&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-172" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-172">&#91;169&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Azerbaijan has diplomatic relations with 158 countries so far and holds membership in 38 international organizations.<sup id="cite_ref-FCO_26-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FCO-26">&#91;23&#93;</a></sup> It holds observer status in the <a href="/wiki/Non-Aligned_Movement" title="Non-Aligned Movement">Non-Aligned Movement</a> and <a href="/wiki/World_Trade_Organization" title="World Trade Organization">World Trade Organization</a> and is a correspondent at the <a href="/wiki/International_Telecommunication_Union" title="International Telecommunication Union">International Telecommunication Union</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-FCO_26-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FCO-26">&#91;23&#93;</a></sup> 
</p><p>On 9 May 2006 Azerbaijan was elected to membership in the newly established <a href="/wiki/Human_Rights_Council" class="mw-redirect" title="Human Rights Council">Human Rights Council</a> by the <a href="/wiki/United_Nations_General_Assembly" title="United Nations General Assembly">United Nations General Assembly</a>. The term of office began on 19 June 2006.<sup id="cite_ref-173" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-173">&#91;170&#93;</a></sup> Azerbaijan was first elected as a non-permanent member of the <a href="/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council_election,_2011" class="mw-redirect" title="United Nations Security Council election, 2011">UN Security Council in 2011</a> with the support of 155 countries.
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Heads_of_state_attended_ceremony_to_release_young_sturgeons_into_Caspian_Sea_2.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/29/Heads_of_state_attended_ceremony_to_release_young_sturgeons_into_Caspian_Sea_2.jpg/220px-Heads_of_state_attended_ceremony_to_release_young_sturgeons_into_Caspian_Sea_2.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/29/Heads_of_state_attended_ceremony_to_release_young_sturgeons_into_Caspian_Sea_2.jpg/330px-Heads_of_state_attended_ceremony_to_release_young_sturgeons_into_Caspian_Sea_2.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/29/Heads_of_state_attended_ceremony_to_release_young_sturgeons_into_Caspian_Sea_2.jpg/440px-Heads_of_state_attended_ceremony_to_release_young_sturgeons_into_Caspian_Sea_2.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1340" data-file-height="894" /></a><figcaption>President <a href="/wiki/Ilham_Aliyev" title="Ilham Aliyev">Ilham Aliyev</a> and other heads of state hosted by Kazakh President <a href="/wiki/Nursultan_Nazarbayev" title="Nursultan Nazarbayev">Nursultan Nazarbayev</a> at the <a href="/wiki/Caspian_Summit" title="Caspian Summit">Caspian Summit</a> in <a href="/wiki/Aktau" title="Aktau">Aktau</a>, <a href="/wiki/Kazakhstan" title="Kazakhstan">Kazakhstan</a>, August 12, 2018</figcaption></figure>
<p>Foreign policy priorities of Azerbaijan include, first of all, the restoration of its territorial integrity; elimination of the consequences of occupation of Nagorno-Karabakh and seven other regions of Azerbaijan surrounding Nagorno-Karabakh;<sup id="cite_ref-NSC_AZ_174-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NSC_AZ-174">&#91;171&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-175" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-175">&#91;172&#93;</a></sup> integration into European and Euro-Atlantic structure; contribution to international security; cooperation with international organizations; regional cooperation and bilateral relations; strengthening of defense capability; promotion of security by domestic policy means; strengthening of democracy; preservation of ethnic and religious tolerance; scientific, educational, and cultural policy and preservation of moral values; economic and social development; enhancing internal and border security; and migration, energy, and transportation security policy.<sup id="cite_ref-NSC_AZ_174-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NSC_AZ-174">&#91;171&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Azerbaijan is an active member of international coalitions fighting international terrorism, and was one of the first countries to offer support after the <a href="/wiki/September_11_attacks" title="September 11 attacks">September 11 attacks</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-176" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-176">&#91;173&#93;</a></sup> The country is an active member of <a href="/wiki/NATO" title="NATO">NATO</a>'s <a href="/wiki/Partnership_for_Peace" title="Partnership for Peace">Partnership for Peace</a> program, contributing to peacekeeping efforts in Kosovo, Afghanistan and Iraq.<sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (September 2023)">citation needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup> Azerbaijan is also a <a href="/wiki/Member_states_of_the_Council_of_Europe" title="Member states of the Council of Europe">member</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Council_of_Europe" title="Council of Europe">Council of Europe</a> since 2001 and maintains good relations with the <a href="/wiki/European_Union" title="European Union">European Union</a>. The country may eventually apply for EU membership.<sup id="cite_ref-NSC_AZ_174-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NSC_AZ-174">&#91;171&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Ilham_Aliyev,_President_of_European_Council_Charles_Michel_held_one-on-one_meeting_in_Brussels_01.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3f/Ilham_Aliyev%2C_President_of_European_Council_Charles_Michel_held_one-on-one_meeting_in_Brussels_01.jpg/220px-Ilham_Aliyev%2C_President_of_European_Council_Charles_Michel_held_one-on-one_meeting_in_Brussels_01.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="137" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3f/Ilham_Aliyev%2C_President_of_European_Council_Charles_Michel_held_one-on-one_meeting_in_Brussels_01.jpg/330px-Ilham_Aliyev%2C_President_of_European_Council_Charles_Michel_held_one-on-one_meeting_in_Brussels_01.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3f/Ilham_Aliyev%2C_President_of_European_Council_Charles_Michel_held_one-on-one_meeting_in_Brussels_01.jpg/440px-Ilham_Aliyev%2C_President_of_European_Council_Charles_Michel_held_one-on-one_meeting_in_Brussels_01.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1960" data-file-height="1220" /></a><figcaption>President <a href="/wiki/Ilham_Aliyev" title="Ilham Aliyev">Ilham Aliyev</a> and President of the <a href="/wiki/European_Council" title="European Council">European Council</a> <a href="/wiki/Charles_Michel" title="Charles Michel">Charles Michel</a> in <a href="/wiki/Brussels" title="Brussels">Brussels</a>, <a href="/wiki/Belgium" title="Belgium">Belgium</a>, April 6, 2022</figcaption></figure> 
<p>On 1 July 2021, the US Congress advanced legislation that will have an impact on the military aid that Washington has sent to Azerbaijan since 2012. This was due to the fact that the packages to <a href="/wiki/Armenia" title="Armenia">Armenia</a>, instead, are significantly smaller.<sup id="cite_ref-177" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-177">&#91;174&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Azerbaijan has been harshly criticized for bribing foreign officials and diplomats to promote its causes abroad and legitimize its elections at home, a practice termed <a href="/wiki/Caviar_diplomacy" title="Caviar diplomacy">caviar diplomacy</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-178" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-178">&#91;175&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-179" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-179">&#91;176&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-180" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-180">&#91;177&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-181" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-181">&#91;178&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijani_laundromat" title="Azerbaijani laundromat">Azerbaijani laundromat</a> <a href="/wiki/Money_laundering" title="Money laundering">money laundering</a> operation involved the bribery of foreign politicians and journalists to serve the Azerbaijani government's public relations interests.<sup id="cite_ref-182" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-182">&#91;179&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Military">Military</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijani_Armed_Forces" title="Azerbaijani Armed Forces">Azerbaijani Armed Forces</a></div>
<figure class="mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Ilham_Aliyev_and_Recep_Tayyip_Erdogan_attended_TEKNOFEST_Azerbaijan_festival_in_Baku_46.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8f/Ilham_Aliyev_and_Recep_Tayyip_Erdogan_attended_TEKNOFEST_Azerbaijan_festival_in_Baku_46.jpg/250px-Ilham_Aliyev_and_Recep_Tayyip_Erdogan_attended_TEKNOFEST_Azerbaijan_festival_in_Baku_46.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="145" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8f/Ilham_Aliyev_and_Recep_Tayyip_Erdogan_attended_TEKNOFEST_Azerbaijan_festival_in_Baku_46.jpg/375px-Ilham_Aliyev_and_Recep_Tayyip_Erdogan_attended_TEKNOFEST_Azerbaijan_festival_in_Baku_46.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8f/Ilham_Aliyev_and_Recep_Tayyip_Erdogan_attended_TEKNOFEST_Azerbaijan_festival_in_Baku_46.jpg/500px-Ilham_Aliyev_and_Recep_Tayyip_Erdogan_attended_TEKNOFEST_Azerbaijan_festival_in_Baku_46.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1960" data-file-height="1135" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Azerbaijani_Navy" title="Azerbaijani Navy">Azerbaijani Navy</a> ships during the 2022 Teknofest Azerbaijan festival in <a href="/wiki/Baku" title="Baku">Baku</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>The history of the modern Azerbaijan army dates back to <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijan_Democratic_Republic" title="Azerbaijan Democratic Republic">Azerbaijan Democratic Republic</a> in 1918 when the National Army of the newly formed Azerbaijan Democratic Republic was created on 26 June 1918.<sup id="cite_ref-183" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-183">&#91;180&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-184" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-184">&#91;181&#93;</a></sup> When Azerbaijan gained independence after the <a href="/wiki/Dissolution_of_the_Soviet_Union" title="Dissolution of the Soviet Union">dissolution of the Soviet Union</a>, the Armed Forces of the Republic of Azerbaijan were created according to the Law on the Armed Forces of 9 October 1991.<sup id="cite_ref-185" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-185">&#91;182&#93;</a></sup> The original date of the establishment of the short-lived National Army is celebrated as Army Day (26 June) in today's Azerbaijan.<sup id="cite_ref-186" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-186">&#91;183&#93;</a></sup>
As of 2021, Azerbaijan had 126,000 active personnel in its armed forces. There are also 17,000 paramilitary troops and 330,00 reserve personnel.<sup id="cite_ref-Blandy12_187-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Blandy12-187">&#91;184&#93;</a></sup> The armed forces have three branches: the <a href="/wiki/Army_of_Azerbaijan" class="mw-redirect" title="Army of Azerbaijan">Land Forces</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijani_Air_Forces" title="Azerbaijani Air Forces">Air Forces</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijan_Navy" class="mw-redirect" title="Azerbaijan Navy">Navy</a>. Additionally the armed forces embrace several military sub-groups that can be involved in state defense when needed. These are the <a href="/wiki/Internal_Troops_(Azerbaijan)" class="mw-redirect" title="Internal Troops (Azerbaijan)">Internal Troops</a> of the Ministry of Internal Affairs and the <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijan_Border_Guard" class="mw-redirect" title="Azerbaijan Border Guard">State Border Service</a>, which includes the <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijan_Coast_Guard" class="mw-redirect" title="Azerbaijan Coast Guard">Coast Guard</a> as well.<sup id="cite_ref-cia_28-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cia-28">&#91;25&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijan_National_Guard" class="mw-redirect" title="Azerbaijan National Guard">Azerbaijan National Guard</a> is a further paramilitary force. It operates as a semi-independent entity of the Special State Protection Service, an agency subordinate to the President.<sup id="cite_ref-188" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-188">&#91;185&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Servicemen_of_the_%22Yarasa%22_Special_Forces_at_Victory_Parade_in_Baku.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/aa/Servicemen_of_the_%22Yarasa%22_Special_Forces_at_Victory_Parade_in_Baku.jpg/220px-Servicemen_of_the_%22Yarasa%22_Special_Forces_at_Victory_Parade_in_Baku.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="146" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/aa/Servicemen_of_the_%22Yarasa%22_Special_Forces_at_Victory_Parade_in_Baku.jpg/330px-Servicemen_of_the_%22Yarasa%22_Special_Forces_at_Victory_Parade_in_Baku.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/aa/Servicemen_of_the_%22Yarasa%22_Special_Forces_at_Victory_Parade_in_Baku.jpg/440px-Servicemen_of_the_%22Yarasa%22_Special_Forces_at_Victory_Parade_in_Baku.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1944" data-file-height="1292" /></a><figcaption>Members of the <a href="/wiki/Special_Forces_of_Azerbaijan" title="Special Forces of Azerbaijan">Special Forces of Azerbaijan</a> during the <a href="/wiki/Baku_Victory_Parade_of_2020" title="Baku Victory Parade of 2020">Baku Victory Parade of 2020</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>Azerbaijan adheres to the <a href="/wiki/Treaty_on_Conventional_Armed_Forces_in_Europe" title="Treaty on Conventional Armed Forces in Europe">Treaty on Conventional Armed Forces in Europe</a> and has signed all major international arms and weapons treaties. Azerbaijan closely cooperates with <a href="/wiki/NATO" title="NATO">NATO</a> in programs such as <a href="/wiki/Partnership_for_Peace" title="Partnership for Peace">Partnership for Peace</a> and <a href="/wiki/Individual_Partnership_Action_Plan" title="Individual Partnership Action Plan">Individual Partnership Action Plan/pfp and ipa</a>. Azerbaijan has deployed 151 of its Peacekeeping Forces in Iraq and another 184 in Afghanistan.<sup id="cite_ref-189" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-189">&#91;186&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Azerbaijan spent $2.24 billion on its defence budget as of 2020<sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><a class="external text" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Azerbaijan&amp;action=edit">&#91;update&#93;</a></sup>,<sup id="cite_ref-190" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-190">&#91;187&#93;</a></sup> which amounted to 5.4% of its total GDP,<sup id="cite_ref-191" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-191">&#91;188&#93;</a></sup> and some 12.7% of general government expenditure.<sup id="cite_ref-192" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-192">&#91;189&#93;</a></sup> Azerbaijani <a href="/wiki/Ministry_of_Defence_Industry_of_Azerbaijan" title="Ministry of Defence Industry of Azerbaijan">defense industry</a> manufactures small arms, artillery systems, tanks, armors and <a href="/wiki/Night_vision_device" class="mw-redirect" title="Night vision device">night vision devices</a>, aviation bombs, UAV'S/unmanned aerial vehicle, various military vehicles and military planes and helicopters.<sup id="cite_ref-193" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-193">&#91;190&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-194" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-194">&#91;191&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-195" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-195">&#91;192&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-196" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-196">&#91;193&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Administrative_divisions">Administrative divisions</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Administrative_divisions_of_Azerbaijan" title="Administrative divisions of Azerbaijan">Administrative divisions of Azerbaijan</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Economic_Regions_of_Azerbaijan_(2021;_labelled).png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/64/Economic_Regions_of_Azerbaijan_%282021%3B_labelled%29.png/400px-Economic_Regions_of_Azerbaijan_%282021%3B_labelled%29.png" decoding="async" width="400" height="304" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/64/Economic_Regions_of_Azerbaijan_%282021%3B_labelled%29.png/600px-Economic_Regions_of_Azerbaijan_%282021%3B_labelled%29.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/64/Economic_Regions_of_Azerbaijan_%282021%3B_labelled%29.png/800px-Economic_Regions_of_Azerbaijan_%282021%3B_labelled%29.png 2x" data-file-width="970" data-file-height="738" /></a><figcaption>Azerbaijan is divided into 14 economic regions.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Azerbaijan is administratively divided into 14 economic regions; 66 <a href="/wiki/Raion" title="Raion">rayons</a> (<span title="Azerbaijani-language text"><i lang="az">rayonlar</i></span>, singular <span title="Azerbaijani-language text"><i lang="az">rayon</i></span>) and 11 cities (<span title="Azerbaijani-language text"><i lang="az">şəhərlər</i></span>, singular <span title="Azerbaijani-language text"><i lang="az">şəhər</i></span>) under the direct authority of the republic.<sup id="cite_ref-197" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-197">&#91;194&#93;</a></sup> Moreover, Azerbaijan includes the <a href="/wiki/Autonomous_Republic" class="mw-redirect" title="Autonomous Republic">Autonomous Republic</a> (<span title="Azerbaijani-language text"><i lang="az">muxtar respublika</i></span>) of <a href="/wiki/Nakhchivan_Autonomous_Republic" title="Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic">Nakhchivan</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-cia_28-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cia-28">&#91;25&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/President_of_Azerbaijan" title="President of Azerbaijan">President of Azerbaijan</a> appoints the governors of these units, while the government of Nakhchivan is elected and approved by the parliament of Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic.
</p>

<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Economy">Economy</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Economy_of_Azerbaijan" title="Economy of Azerbaijan">Economy of Azerbaijan</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:GPD_per_capita_development_of_Azerbaijan.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/88/GPD_per_capita_development_of_Azerbaijan.jpg/220px-GPD_per_capita_development_of_Azerbaijan.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="139" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/88/GPD_per_capita_development_of_Azerbaijan.jpg/330px-GPD_per_capita_development_of_Azerbaijan.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/88/GPD_per_capita_development_of_Azerbaijan.jpg/440px-GPD_per_capita_development_of_Azerbaijan.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1031" data-file-height="650" /></a><figcaption>Change in per capita GDP of Azerbaijan since 1973. Figures are inflation-adjusted to 2011 International dollars.</figcaption></figure>
<p>After gaining independence in 1991, Azerbaijan became a member of the <a href="/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund" title="International Monetary Fund">International Monetary Fund</a>, the <a href="/wiki/World_Bank" title="World Bank">World Bank</a>, the <a href="/wiki/European_Bank_for_Reconstruction_and_Development" title="European Bank for Reconstruction and Development">European Bank for Reconstruction and Development</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Islamic_Development_Bank" title="Islamic Development Bank">Islamic Development Bank</a>, and the <a href="/wiki/Asian_Development_Bank" title="Asian Development Bank">Asian Development Bank</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-AZE_199-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-AZE-199">&#91;195&#93;</a></sup> The banking system of Azerbaijan consists of the <a href="/wiki/Central_Bank_of_Azerbaijan" title="Central Bank of Azerbaijan">Central Bank of Azerbaijan</a>, <a href="/wiki/Commercial_bank" title="Commercial bank">commercial banks</a>, and non-banking credit organizations. The National (now Central) Bank was created in 1992 based on the Azerbaijan State Savings Bank, an affiliate of the former State Savings Bank of the USSR. The Central Bank serves as Azerbaijan's central bank, empowered to issue the national currency, the <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijani_manat" title="Azerbaijani manat">Azerbaijani manat</a>, and to supervise all commercial banks. Two major commercial banks are <a href="/wiki/Unibank_(Azerbaijan)" title="Unibank (Azerbaijan)">UniBank</a> and the state-owned <a href="/wiki/International_Bank_of_Azerbaijan" title="International Bank of Azerbaijan">International Bank of Azerbaijan</a>, run by Abbas Ibrahimov.<sup id="cite_ref-200" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-200">&#91;196&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Pushed up by spending and demand growth, the 2007 <a href="/wiki/First_quarter_of_a_calendar_year" class="mw-redirect" title="First quarter of a calendar year">Q1</a> inflation rate reached 16.6%.<sup id="cite_ref-INF_201-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-INF-201">&#91;197&#93;</a></sup> Nominal incomes and monthly wages climbed 29% and 25% respectively against this figure, but price increases in the non-oil industry encouraged inflation.<sup id="cite_ref-INF_201-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-INF-201">&#91;197&#93;</a></sup> Azerbaijan shows some signs of the so-called "<a href="/wiki/Dutch_disease" title="Dutch disease">Dutch disease</a>" because of its fast-growing energy sector, which causes inflation and makes non-energy exports more expensive.<sup id="cite_ref-202" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-202">&#91;198&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Azerbaijan_Product_Exports_(2019).svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/84/Azerbaijan_Product_Exports_%282019%29.svg/310px-Azerbaijan_Product_Exports_%282019%29.svg.png" decoding="async" width="310" height="202" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/84/Azerbaijan_Product_Exports_%282019%29.svg/465px-Azerbaijan_Product_Exports_%282019%29.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/84/Azerbaijan_Product_Exports_%282019%29.svg/620px-Azerbaijan_Product_Exports_%282019%29.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="1100" data-file-height="715" /></a><figcaption>A proportional representation of Azerbaijan exports, 2019</figcaption></figure>
<p>In the early 2000s, chronically high inflation was brought under control. This led to the launch of a new currency, the new Azerbaijani manat, on 1 January 2006, to cement the economic reforms and erase the vestiges of an unstable economy.<sup id="cite_ref-203" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-203">&#91;199&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-204" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-204">&#91;200&#93;</a></sup>
Azerbaijan is also ranked 57th in the <a href="/wiki/Global_Competitiveness_Report" title="Global Competitiveness Report">Global Competitiveness Report</a> for 2010–2011, above other CIS countries.<sup id="cite_ref-205" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-205">&#91;201&#93;</a></sup> By 2012 the <a href="/wiki/Gross_domestic_product" title="Gross domestic product">GDP</a> of Azerbaijan had increased 20-fold from its 1995 level.<sup id="cite_ref-206" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-206">&#91;202&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Energy_and_natural_resources">Energy and natural resources</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Energy_in_Azerbaijan" title="Energy in Azerbaijan">Energy in Azerbaijan</a></div> <link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/Petroleum_industry_in_Azerbaijan" title="Petroleum industry in Azerbaijan">Petroleum industry in Azerbaijan</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Oil_Rocks_near_Baku.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0f/Oil_Rocks_near_Baku.jpg/220px-Oil_Rocks_near_Baku.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0f/Oil_Rocks_near_Baku.jpg/330px-Oil_Rocks_near_Baku.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0f/Oil_Rocks_near_Baku.jpg/440px-Oil_Rocks_near_Baku.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1536" data-file-height="1024" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Oil_Rocks" class="mw-redirect" title="Oil Rocks">Oil Rocks</a> (Neft Daşları) near Baku</figcaption></figure>
<p>Two-thirds of Azerbaijan is rich in oil and natural gas.<sup id="cite_ref-AZ_207-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-AZ-207">&#91;203&#93;</a></sup>
The history of the oil industry of Azerbaijan dates back to the ancient period. Arabian historian and traveler <a href="/wiki/Al-Baladhuri" title="Al-Baladhuri">Ahmad Al-Baladhuri</a> discussed the economy of the Absheron peninsula in antiquity, mentioning its oil in particular.<sup id="cite_ref-208" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-208">&#91;204&#93;</a></sup> There are many <a href="/wiki/Pipelines_in_Azerbaijan" title="Pipelines in Azerbaijan">pipelines in Azerbaijan</a>. The goal of the <a href="/wiki/Southern_Gas_Corridor" title="Southern Gas Corridor">Southern Gas Corridor</a>, which connects the giant <a href="/wiki/Shah_Deniz_gas_field" title="Shah Deniz gas field">Shah Deniz gas field</a> in Azerbaijan to Europe,<sup id="cite_ref-naturalgas_209-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-naturalgas-209">&#91;205&#93;</a></sup> is to reduce European Union's dependency on Russian gas.<sup id="cite_ref-210" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-210">&#91;206&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The region of the <a href="/wiki/Lesser_Caucasus" title="Lesser Caucasus">Lesser Caucasus</a> accounts for most of the country's gold, silver, iron, copper, <a href="/wiki/Titanium" title="Titanium">titanium</a>, <a href="/wiki/Chromium" title="Chromium">chromium</a>, <a href="/wiki/Manganese" title="Manganese">manganese</a>, <a href="/wiki/Cobalt" title="Cobalt">cobalt</a>, <a href="/wiki/Molybdenum" title="Molybdenum">molybdenum</a>, complex <a href="/wiki/Ore" title="Ore">ore</a> and <a href="/wiki/Antimony" title="Antimony">antimony</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-AZ_207-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-AZ-207">&#91;203&#93;</a></sup> In September 1994, a 30-year contract was signed between the <a href="/wiki/State_Oil_Company_of_Azerbaijan_Republic" class="mw-redirect" title="State Oil Company of Azerbaijan Republic">State Oil Company of Azerbaijan Republic</a> (SOCAR) and 13&#160;oil companies, among them <a href="/wiki/Amoco" title="Amoco">Amoco</a>, <a href="/wiki/BP" title="BP">BP</a>, <a href="/wiki/ExxonMobil" title="ExxonMobil">ExxonMobil</a>, <a href="/wiki/Lukoil" title="Lukoil">Lukoil</a> and <a href="/wiki/Equinor" title="Equinor">Equinor</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-AZE_199-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-AZE-199">&#91;195&#93;</a></sup> As Western oil companies are able to tap deepwater <a href="/wiki/Oil_field" class="mw-redirect" title="Oil field">oilfields</a> untouched by the Soviet exploitation, Azerbaijan is considered one of the most important spots in the world for <a href="/wiki/Hydrocarbon_exploration" title="Hydrocarbon exploration">oil exploration</a> and development.<sup id="cite_ref-211" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-211">&#91;207&#93;</a></sup> Meanwhile, the <a href="/wiki/State_Oil_Fund_of_Azerbaijan" title="State Oil Fund of Azerbaijan">State Oil Fund of Azerbaijan</a> was established as an extra-budgetary fund to ensure <a href="/wiki/Macroeconomy" class="mw-redirect" title="Macroeconomy">macroeconomic</a> stability, transparency in the management of oil revenue, and safeguarding of resources for future generations.
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Baku_pipelines.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/Baku_pipelines.svg/300px-Baku_pipelines.svg.png" decoding="async" width="300" height="174" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/Baku_pipelines.svg/450px-Baku_pipelines.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/Baku_pipelines.svg/600px-Baku_pipelines.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="1316" data-file-height="762" /></a><figcaption>The <a href="/wiki/South_Caucasus_Pipeline" title="South Caucasus Pipeline">South Caucasus Pipeline</a> is bringing natural gas through Turkey to Europe.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Access to <a href="/wiki/Biocapacity" title="Biocapacity">biocapacity</a> in Azerbaijan is less than world average. In 2016, Azerbaijan had 0.8 global hectares<sup id="cite_ref-footprintdata_212-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-footprintdata-212">&#91;208&#93;</a></sup> of biocapacity per person within its territory, half the world average of 1.6 global hectares per person.<sup id="cite_ref-213" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-213">&#91;209&#93;</a></sup> In 2016 Azerbaijan used 2.1 global hectares of biocapacity per person&#160;– their <a href="/wiki/Ecological_footprint" title="Ecological footprint">ecological footprint</a> of consumption. This means they use more biocapacity than Azerbaijan contains. As a result, Azerbaijan is running a biocapacity deficit.<sup id="cite_ref-footprintdata_212-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-footprintdata-212">&#91;208&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Azeriqaz, a sub-company of SOCAR, intends to ensure full gasification of the country by 2021.<sup id="cite_ref-214" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-214">&#91;210&#93;</a></sup>
Azerbaijan is one of the sponsors of the east–west and north–south energy transport corridors. <a href="/wiki/Baku%E2%80%93Tbilisi%E2%80%93Kars_railway" title="Baku–Tbilisi–Kars railway">Baku–Tbilisi–Kars railway</a> line will connect the Caspian region with Turkey, which is expected to be completed in July 2017. The <a href="/wiki/Trans-Anatolian_gas_pipeline" title="Trans-Anatolian gas pipeline">Trans-Anatolian gas pipeline</a> (TANAP) and <a href="/wiki/Trans_Adriatic_Pipeline" title="Trans Adriatic Pipeline">Trans Adriatic Pipeline</a> (TAP) will deliver natural gas from Azerbaijan's Shah Deniz gas to Turkey and Europe.<sup id="cite_ref-naturalgas_209-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-naturalgas-209">&#91;205&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Azerbaijan extended the agreement on development of <a href="/wiki/Azeri%E2%80%93Chirag%E2%80%93Gunashli" title="Azeri–Chirag–Gunashli">ACG</a> until 2050 according to the amended <a href="/wiki/Production_sharing_agreement" title="Production sharing agreement">PSA</a> signed on 14 September 2017 by <a href="/wiki/SOCAR" title="SOCAR">SOCAR</a> and co-ventures (<a href="/wiki/BP" title="BP">BP</a>, <a href="/wiki/Chevron_Corporation" title="Chevron Corporation">Chevron</a>, <a href="/wiki/Inpex" title="Inpex">Inpex</a>, <a href="/wiki/Equinor" title="Equinor">Equinor</a>, <a href="/wiki/ExxonMobil" title="ExxonMobil">ExxonMobil</a>, <a href="/wiki/T%C3%BCrkiye_Petrolleri_Anonim_Ortakl%C4%B1%C4%9F%C4%B1" class="mw-redirect" title="Türkiye Petrolleri Anonim Ortaklığı">TP</a>, ITOCHU and <a href="/wiki/Oil_and_Natural_Gas_Corporation" title="Oil and Natural Gas Corporation">ONGC Videsh</a>).<sup id="cite_ref-215" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-215">&#91;211&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Agriculture">Agriculture</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Agriculture_in_Azerbaijan" title="Agriculture in Azerbaijan">Agriculture in Azerbaijan</a></div>
<p>Azerbaijan has the largest agricultural basin in the region. About 54.9 percent of Azerbaijan is agricultural land.<sup id="cite_ref-STA_133-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-STA-133">&#91;130&#93;</a></sup> At the beginning of 2007 there were 4,755,100&#160;hectares of utilized agricultural area.<sup id="cite_ref-AG_216-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-AG-216">&#91;212&#93;</a></sup> In the same year the total wood resources counted 136&#160;million m<sup>3</sup>.<sup id="cite_ref-AG_216-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-AG-216">&#91;212&#93;</a></sup> Azerbaijan's agricultural scientific research institutes are focused on meadows and pastures, horticulture and <a href="/wiki/Subtropical" class="mw-redirect" title="Subtropical">subtropical</a> crops, green vegetables, <a href="/wiki/Viticulture" title="Viticulture">viticulture</a> and <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijani_wine" title="Azerbaijani wine">wine-making</a>, cotton growing and <a href="/wiki/Medicinal_plants" title="Medicinal plants">medicinal plants</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-217" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-217">&#91;213&#93;</a></sup> In some areas it is profitable to grow grain, potatoes, <a href="/wiki/Sugar_beet" title="Sugar beet">sugar beets</a>, cotton<sup id="cite_ref-218" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-218">&#91;214&#93;</a></sup> and tobacco. Livestock, dairy products, and wine and <a href="/wiki/Distilled_spirit" class="mw-redirect" title="Distilled spirit">spirits</a> are also important farm products. The Caspian <a href="/wiki/Fishing_industry" title="Fishing industry">fishing industry</a> concentrates on the dwindling stocks of <a href="/wiki/Sturgeon" title="Sturgeon">sturgeon</a> and <a href="/wiki/Beluga_(sturgeon)" title="Beluga (sturgeon)">beluga</a>. In 2002 the Azerbaijani <a href="/wiki/Merchant_marine" class="mw-redirect" title="Merchant marine">merchant marine</a> had 54 ships.<sup id="cite_ref-219" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-219">&#91;215&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Some products previously imported from abroad have begun to be produced locally. Among them are Coca-Cola by Coca-Cola Bottlers LTD., beer by Baki-Kastel, parquet by Nehir and oil pipes by EUPEC Pipe Coating Azerbaijan.<sup id="cite_ref-220" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-220">&#91;216&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Tourism">Tourism</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Tourism_in_Azerbaijan" title="Tourism in Azerbaijan">Tourism in Azerbaijan</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Shahdag01.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/59/Shahdag01.jpg/220px-Shahdag01.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/59/Shahdag01.jpg/330px-Shahdag01.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/59/Shahdag01.jpg/440px-Shahdag01.jpg 2x" data-file-width="7360" data-file-height="4912" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Shahdag_Mountain_Resort" title="Shahdag Mountain Resort">Shahdag Mountain Resort</a> is the country's largest winter resort.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Tourism is an important part of the <a href="/wiki/Economy_of_Azerbaijan" title="Economy of Azerbaijan">economy of Azerbaijan</a>. The country was a well-known tourist spot in the 1980s. The fall of the Soviet Union, and the <a href="/wiki/First_Nagorno-Karabakh_War" title="First Nagorno-Karabakh War">First Nagorno-Karabakh War</a> during the 1990s, damaged the tourist industry and the image of Azerbaijan as a tourist destination.<sup id="cite_ref-221" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-221">&#91;217&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>It was not until the 2000s that the tourism industry began to recover, and the country has since experienced a high rate of growth in the number of tourist visits and overnight stays.<sup id="cite_ref-222" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-222">&#91;218&#93;</a></sup> 
</p><p>In recent years, Azerbaijan has also become a popular destination for religious, spa, and <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijani_medical_tourism" class="mw-redirect" title="Azerbaijani medical tourism">health care tourism</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Baku_Boom_Has_Yet_to_Hit_Regions_223-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Baku_Boom_Has_Yet_to_Hit_Regions-223">&#91;219&#93;</a></sup> During winter, the <a href="/wiki/Shahdag_Mountain_Resort" title="Shahdag Mountain Resort">Shahdag Mountain Resort</a> offers skiing with state of the art facilities.<sup id="cite_ref-224" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-224">&#91;220&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Modern_Baku_seen_from_the_Martyrs%27_Memorial_(37068871235).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2e/Modern_Baku_seen_from_the_Martyrs%27_Memorial_%2837068871235%29.jpg/220px-Modern_Baku_seen_from_the_Martyrs%27_Memorial_%2837068871235%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2e/Modern_Baku_seen_from_the_Martyrs%27_Memorial_%2837068871235%29.jpg/330px-Modern_Baku_seen_from_the_Martyrs%27_Memorial_%2837068871235%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2e/Modern_Baku_seen_from_the_Martyrs%27_Memorial_%2837068871235%29.jpg/440px-Modern_Baku_seen_from_the_Martyrs%27_Memorial_%2837068871235%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4608" data-file-height="3456" /></a><figcaption>Port of <a href="/wiki/Baku" title="Baku">Baku</a> on the <a href="/wiki/Caspian_Sea" title="Caspian Sea">Caspian Sea</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>The <a href="/wiki/Government_of_Azerbaijan" class="mw-redirect" title="Government of Azerbaijan">government of Azerbaijan</a> has set the development of Azerbaijan as an elite tourist destination as a top priority. It is a national strategy to make tourism a major, if not the single largest, contributor to the Azerbaijani economy.<sup id="cite_ref-225" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-225">&#91;221&#93;</a></sup> These activities are regulated by the <a href="/wiki/Ministry_of_Culture_and_Tourism_(Azerbaijan)" class="mw-redirect" title="Ministry of Culture and Tourism (Azerbaijan)">Ministry of Culture and Tourism of Azerbaijan</a>.
</p><p>There are 63 countries which have a visa-free score.<sup id="cite_ref-226" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-226">&#91;222&#93;</a></sup>
E-visa<sup id="cite_ref-227" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-227">&#91;223&#93;</a></sup> – for a visit of foreigners of visa-required countries to the Republic of Azerbaijan.
</p><p>According to the Travel and Tourism Competitiveness Report 2015 of the World Economic Forum, Azerbaijan holds 84th place.<sup id="cite_ref-228" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-228">&#91;224&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>According to a report by the World Travel and Tourism Council, Azerbaijan was among the top ten countries showing the strongest growth in visitor exports between 2010 and 2016,<sup id="cite_ref-229" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-229">&#91;225&#93;</a></sup> In addition, Azerbaijan placed first (46.1%) among countries with the fastest-developing travel and tourism economies, with strong indicators for inbound international visitor spending last year.<sup id="cite_ref-230" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-230">&#91;226&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<div class="thumb tnone" style="margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;overflow:hidden;width:auto;max-width:808px"><div class="thumbinner"><div class="noresize" style="overflow:auto"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:Vista_de_Baku,_Azerbaiy%C3%A1n,_2016-09-26,_DD_101-106_PAN.jpg" class="mw-file-description" title="Panoramic view of Baku, the capital and largest city of Azerbaijan"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9c/Vista_de_Baku%2C_Azerbaiy%C3%A1n%2C_2016-09-26%2C_DD_101-106_PAN.jpg/800px-Vista_de_Baku%2C_Azerbaiy%C3%A1n%2C_2016-09-26%2C_DD_101-106_PAN.jpg" decoding="async" width="800" height="187" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9c/Vista_de_Baku%2C_Azerbaiy%C3%A1n%2C_2016-09-26%2C_DD_101-106_PAN.jpg/1200px-Vista_de_Baku%2C_Azerbaiy%C3%A1n%2C_2016-09-26%2C_DD_101-106_PAN.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9c/Vista_de_Baku%2C_Azerbaiy%C3%A1n%2C_2016-09-26%2C_DD_101-106_PAN.jpg/1600px-Vista_de_Baku%2C_Azerbaiy%C3%A1n%2C_2016-09-26%2C_DD_101-106_PAN.jpg 2x" data-file-width="15277" data-file-height="3574" /></a></span></div><div class="thumbcaption" style="text-align:center"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Vista_de_Baku,_Azerbaiy%C3%A1n,_2016-09-26,_DD_101-106_PAN.jpg" title="File:Vista de Baku, Azerbaiyán, 2016-09-26, DD 101-106 PAN.jpg"> </a></div>Panoramic view of <a href="/wiki/Baku" title="Baku">Baku</a>, the capital and largest city of Azerbaijan</div></div></div>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Transportation">Transportation</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Transportation_in_Azerbaijan" class="mw-redirect" title="Transportation in Azerbaijan">Transportation in Azerbaijan</a> and <a href="/wiki/Rail_transport_in_Azerbaijan" title="Rail transport in Azerbaijan">Rail transport in Azerbaijan</a></div>
<p>The convenient location of Azerbaijan on the crossroad of major international traffic arteries, such as the <a href="/wiki/Silk_Road" title="Silk Road">Silk Road</a> and the south–north corridor, highlights the strategic importance of the transportation sector for the country's economy.<sup id="cite_ref-231" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-231">&#91;227&#93;</a></sup> The transport sector in the country includes roads, railways, aviation, and maritime transport.
</p><p>Azerbaijan is also an important economic hub in the transportation of raw materials. The <a href="/wiki/Baku%E2%80%93Tbilisi%E2%80%93Ceyhan_pipeline" title="Baku–Tbilisi–Ceyhan pipeline">Baku–Tbilisi–Ceyhan pipeline</a> (BTC) became operational in May 2006 and extends more than 1,774&#160;km (1,102&#160;mi) through the territories of Azerbaijan, Georgia, and Turkey. The BTC is designed to transport up to 50&#160;million tons of crude oil annually and carries oil from the Caspian Sea oilfields to global markets.<sup id="cite_ref-232" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-232">&#91;228&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/South_Caucasus_Pipeline" title="South Caucasus Pipeline">South Caucasus Pipeline</a>, also stretching through the territory of Azerbaijan, Georgia, and Turkey, became operational at the end of 2006 and offers additional gas supplies to the European market from the <a href="/wiki/Shah_Deniz_gas_field" title="Shah Deniz gas field">Shah Deniz gas field</a>. Shah Deniz is expected to produce up to 296&#160;billion cubic meters of natural gas per year.<sup id="cite_ref-233" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-233">&#91;229&#93;</a></sup> Azerbaijan also plays a major role in the EU-sponsored Silk Road Project.<sup id="cite_ref-234" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-234">&#91;230&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In 2002, the Azerbaijani government established the Ministry of Transport with a broad range of policy and regulatory functions. In the same year, the country became a member of the <a href="/wiki/Vienna_Convention_on_Road_Traffic" title="Vienna Convention on Road Traffic">Vienna Convention on Road Traffic</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-235" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-235">&#91;231&#93;</a></sup> Priorities are upgrading the transport network and improving transportation services to better facilitate the development of other sectors of the economy.<sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (October 2020)">citation needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup>
</p><p>The 2012 construction of <a href="/wiki/Kars%E2%80%93Tbilisi%E2%80%93Baku_railway" class="mw-redirect" title="Kars–Tbilisi–Baku railway">Kars–Tbilisi–Baku railway</a> was meant to improve transportation between Asia and Europe by connecting the railways of China and Kazakhstan in the east to the European railway system in the west via Turkey. In 2010 <a href="/wiki/Russian_gauge" class="mw-redirect" title="Russian gauge">Broad-gauge</a> railways and electrified railways stretched for 2,918&#160;km (1,813&#160;mi) and 1,278&#160;km (794&#160;mi) respectively. By 2010, there were 35 airports and one <a href="/wiki/Heliport" title="Heliport">heliport</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-cia_28-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cia-28">&#91;25&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Science_and_technology">Science and technology</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Science_and_technology_in_Azerbaijan" title="Science and technology in Azerbaijan">Science and technology in Azerbaijan</a>, <a href="/wiki/Communications_in_Azerbaijan" class="mw-redirect" title="Communications in Azerbaijan">Communications in Azerbaijan</a>, <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijan_National_Aerospace_Agency" title="Azerbaijan National Aerospace Agency">Azerbaijan National Aerospace Agency</a>, and <a href="/wiki/List_of_Azerbaijani_inventions_and_discoveries" title="List of Azerbaijani inventions and discoveries">List of Azerbaijani inventions and discoveries</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Shamakhi_observatory.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/76/Shamakhi_observatory.jpg/220px-Shamakhi_observatory.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="146" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/76/Shamakhi_observatory.jpg/330px-Shamakhi_observatory.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/76/Shamakhi_observatory.jpg/440px-Shamakhi_observatory.jpg 2x" data-file-width="500" data-file-height="332" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Shamakhi_Astrophysical_Observatory" class="mw-redirect" title="Shamakhi Astrophysical Observatory">Shamakhi Astrophysical Observatory</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>In the 21st century, a new oil and gas boom helped improve the situation in Azerbaijan's science and technology sectors. The government launched a campaign aimed at modernization and <a href="/wiki/List_of_Azerbaijani_inventions_and_discoveries" title="List of Azerbaijani inventions and discoveries">innovation</a>. The government estimates that profits from the information technology and communication industry will grow and become comparable to those from oil production.<sup id="cite_ref-236" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-236">&#91;232&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Azerbaijan has a large and steadily growing Internet sector, mostly uninfluenced by the <a href="/wiki/Financial_crisis_of_2007%E2%80%932008" class="mw-redirect" title="Financial crisis of 2007–2008">financial crisis of 2007–2008</a>; rapid growth is forecast for at least five more years.<sup id="cite_ref-237" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-237">&#91;233&#93;</a></sup> Azerbaijan was ranked 80th in the <a href="/wiki/Global_Innovation_Index" title="Global Innovation Index">Global Innovation Index</a> in 2021, up from 84th in 2019.<sup id="cite_ref-238" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-238">&#91;234&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-239" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-239">&#91;235&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-240" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-240">&#91;236&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-241" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-241">&#91;237&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The country has also been making progress in developing its telecoms sector. The Ministry of Communications &amp; Information Technologies (MCIT) and an operator through its role in Aztelekom are both policy-makers and regulators. Public payphones are available for local calls and require the purchase of a token from the telephone exchange or some shops and kiosks. Tokens allow a call of indefinite duration. As of 2009<sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><a class="external text" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Azerbaijan&amp;action=edit">&#91;update&#93;</a></sup>, there were 1,397,000 main telephone lines<sup id="cite_ref-242" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-242">&#91;238&#93;</a></sup> and 1,485,000 internet users.<sup id="cite_ref-243" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-243">&#91;239&#93;</a></sup> There are four <a href="/wiki/GSM" title="GSM">GSM</a> providers: <a href="/wiki/Azercell" title="Azercell">Azercell</a>, <a href="/w/index.php?title=Bakcell&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Bakcell (page does not exist)">Bakcell</a><sup class="noprint" style="font-style: normal;">&#160;&#91;<a href="https://az.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bakcell" class="extiw" title="az:Bakcell">az</a>&#93;</sup>, Azerfon (<a href="/wiki/Nar_Mobile" class="mw-redirect" title="Nar Mobile">Nar Mobile</a>), <a href="/wiki/Nakhtel" title="Nakhtel">Nakhtel</a> mobile network operators and one <a href="/wiki/CDMA" class="mw-redirect" title="CDMA">CDMA</a>.
</p><p>In the 21st century a number of prominent Azerbaijani <a href="/wiki/Geodynamics" title="Geodynamics">geodynamics</a> and <a href="/wiki/Geotectonics" class="mw-redirect" title="Geotectonics">geotectonics</a> scientists, inspired by the fundamental works of Elchin Khalilov and others, designed hundreds of earthquake prediction stations and earthquake-resistant buildings that now constitute the bulk of The Republican Center of Seismic Service.<sup id="cite_ref-244" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-244">&#91;240&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-245" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-245">&#91;241&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-246" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-246">&#91;242&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijan_National_Aerospace_Agency" title="Azerbaijan National Aerospace Agency">Azerbaijan National Aerospace Agency</a> launched its first satellite <a href="/wiki/AzerSat_1" class="mw-redirect" title="AzerSat 1">AzerSat 1</a> into orbit on 7 February 2013 from <a href="/wiki/Guiana_Space_Centre" title="Guiana Space Centre">Guiana Space Centre</a> in French Guiana at orbital positions 46° East.<sup id="cite_ref-247" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-247">&#91;243&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-248" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-248">&#91;244&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-249" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-249">&#91;245&#93;</a></sup> The satellite covers Europe and a significant part of Asia and Africa and serves the transmission of TV and radio broadcasting as well as the Internet.<sup id="cite_ref-250" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-250">&#91;246&#93;</a></sup> The launching of a satellite into orbit is Azerbaijan's first step in realizing its goal of becoming a nation with its own space industry, capable of successfully implementing more projects in the future.<sup id="cite_ref-251" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-251">&#91;247&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-252" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-252">&#91;248&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Demographics">Demographics</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Demographics_of_Azerbaijan" title="Demographics of Azerbaijan">Demographics of Azerbaijan</a> and <a href="/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Azerbaijan" title="List of cities in Azerbaijan">List of cities in Azerbaijan</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Azerbaijan_single_age_population_pyramid_2020.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b2/Azerbaijan_single_age_population_pyramid_2020.png/220px-Azerbaijan_single_age_population_pyramid_2020.png" decoding="async" width="220" height="177" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b2/Azerbaijan_single_age_population_pyramid_2020.png/330px-Azerbaijan_single_age_population_pyramid_2020.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b2/Azerbaijan_single_age_population_pyramid_2020.png/440px-Azerbaijan_single_age_population_pyramid_2020.png 2x" data-file-width="2212" data-file-height="1777" /></a><figcaption>Population pyramid</figcaption></figure>
<p>As of March 2022, 52.9% of Azerbaijan's total population of 10,164,464 is <a href="/wiki/Urban_area" title="Urban area">urban</a>, with the remaining 47.1% being rural.<sup id="cite_ref-reportpop_253-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-reportpop-253">&#91;249&#93;</a></sup> In January 2019, the 50.1% of the total population was female. The <a href="/wiki/Human_sex_ratio" title="Human sex ratio">sex ratio</a> in the same year was 0.99 males per female.<sup id="cite_ref-254" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-254">&#91;250&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The 2011 population growth-rate was 0.85%, compared to 1.09% worldwide.<sup id="cite_ref-cia_28-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cia-28">&#91;25&#93;</a></sup> A significant factor restricting population growth is a high level of migration. In 2011 Azerbaijan saw a migration of −1.14/1,000 people.<sup id="cite_ref-cia_28-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cia-28">&#91;25&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijani_diaspora" title="Azerbaijani diaspora">Azerbaijani diaspora</a> is found in 42 countries<sup id="cite_ref-255" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-255">&#91;251&#93;</a></sup> and in turn there are many centers for ethnic minorities inside Azerbaijan, including the <a href="/wiki/Germans_in_Azerbaijan" title="Germans in Azerbaijan">German</a> cultural society "Karelhaus", <a href="/wiki/Slavic_peoples" class="mw-redirect" title="Slavic peoples">Slavic</a> cultural center, Azerbaijani-Israeli community, <a href="/wiki/Kurdish_people" class="mw-redirect" title="Kurdish people">Kurdish</a> cultural center, International <a href="/wiki/Talysh_people" title="Talysh people">Talysh</a> Association, <a href="/wiki/Lezgins" title="Lezgins">Lezgin</a> national center "Samur", Azerbaijani-<a href="/wiki/Tatarstan" title="Tatarstan">Tatar</a> community, <a href="/wiki/Crimean_Tatars" title="Crimean Tatars">Crimean Tatars</a> society, etc.<sup id="cite_ref-MIN_256-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-MIN-256">&#91;252&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In total, Azerbaijan has 78 cities, 63 city districts, and one special legal status city. 261 urban-type settlements and 4248 villages follow these.<sup id="cite_ref-stat.gov.az_257-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-stat.gov.az-257">&#91;253&#93;</a></sup>
</p>

<p>Demographics of Azerbaijan
</p>
<style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r981673959">.mw-parser-output .legend{page-break-inside:avoid;break-inside:avoid-column}.mw-parser-output .legend-color{display:inline-block;min-width:1.25em;height:1.25em;line-height:1.25;margin:1px 0;text-align:center;border:1px solid black;background-color:transparent;color:black}.mw-parser-output .legend-text{}</style><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:green; color:black;">&#160;</span>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Russians" title="Russians">Russians</a> (1.35%)</div><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r981673959"><div class="legend"><span class="legend-color mw-no-invert" style="background-color:red;
