<p>The ethnic composition of the population according to the 2009 population census: 91.6% <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijani_people" class="mw-redirect" title="Azerbaijani people">Azerbaijanis</a>, 2.0% <a href="/wiki/Lezgians" class="mw-redirect" title="Lezgians">Lezgins</a>, 1.4% <a href="/wiki/Armenians" title="Armenians">Armenians</a> (almost all Armenians live in the break-away region of <a href="/wiki/Republic_of_Nagorno-Karabakh" class="mw-redirect" title="Republic of Nagorno-Karabakh">Nagorno-Karabakh</a>), 1.3% <a href="/wiki/Russians" title="Russians">Russians</a>, 1.3% <a href="/wiki/Talysh_people" title="Talysh people">Talysh</a>, 0.6% <a href="/wiki/Caucasian_Avars" class="mw-redirect" title="Caucasian Avars">Avars</a>, 0.4% <a href="/wiki/Turkish_people" title="Turkish people">Turks</a>, 0.3% <a href="/wiki/Tatars" title="Tatars">Tatars</a>, 0.3% <a href="/wiki/Tat_people_(Caucasus)" title="Tat people (Caucasus)">Tats</a>, 0.2% <a href="/wiki/Ukrainians" title="Ukrainians">Ukrainians</a>, 0.1% <a href="/wiki/Tsakhur_people" title="Tsakhur people">Tsakhurs</a>, 0.1% <a href="/wiki/Georgians" title="Georgians">Georgians</a>, 0.1% <a href="/wiki/Jew" class="mw-redirect" title="Jew">Jews</a>, 0.1% <a href="/wiki/Kurdish_people" class="mw-redirect" title="Kurdish people">Kurds</a>, other 0.2%.<sup id="cite_ref-auto_3-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-auto-3">&#91;2&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Languages">Languages</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Languages_of_Azerbaijan" title="Languages of Azerbaijan">Languages of Azerbaijan</a></div>
<p>The official language is <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijani_language" title="Azerbaijani language">Azerbaijani</a>, which is a <a href="/wiki/Turkic_languages" title="Turkic languages">Turkic language</a>. Azerbaijani is spoken by approximately 92% of the population as a <a href="/wiki/Mother_tongue" class="mw-redirect" title="Mother tongue">mother tongue</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-UNLANGDATA_258-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-UNLANGDATA-258">&#91;254&#93;</a></sup> Russian and <a href="/wiki/Armenian_language" title="Armenian language">Armenian</a> (only in Nagorno-Karabakh) are also spoken, and each are the mother tongue of around 1.5% of the population respectively.<sup id="cite_ref-UNLANGDATA_258-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-UNLANGDATA-258">&#91;254&#93;</a></sup> There are a dozen other minority languages spoken natively in the country.<sup id="cite_ref-259" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-259">&#91;255&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Avar_language" title="Avar language">Avar</a>, <a href="/wiki/Budukh_language" title="Budukh language">Budukh</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-Encyclopedia_of_the_World&#39;s_Endangered_Languages_260-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Encyclopedia_of_the_World&#39;s_Endangered_Languages-260">&#91;256&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Georgian_language" title="Georgian language">Georgian</a>, <a href="/wiki/Juhuri_language" class="mw-redirect" title="Juhuri language">Juhuri</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-Encyclopedia_of_the_World&#39;s_Endangered_Languages_260-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Encyclopedia_of_the_World&#39;s_Endangered_Languages-260">&#91;256&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Khinalug_language" title="Khinalug language">Khinalug</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-Encyclopedia_of_the_World&#39;s_Endangered_Languages_260-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Encyclopedia_of_the_World&#39;s_Endangered_Languages-260">&#91;256&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Kryts_language" title="Kryts language">Kryts</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-Encyclopedia_of_the_World&#39;s_Endangered_Languages_260-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Encyclopedia_of_the_World&#39;s_Endangered_Languages-260">&#91;256&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Lezgian_language" title="Lezgian language">Lezgin</a>, <a href="/wiki/Rutul_language" title="Rutul language">Rutul</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-Encyclopedia_of_the_World&#39;s_Endangered_Languages_260-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Encyclopedia_of_the_World&#39;s_Endangered_Languages-260">&#91;256&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Talysh_language" title="Talysh language">Talysh</a>, <a href="/wiki/Tat_language_(Caucasus)" title="Tat language (Caucasus)">Tat</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-Encyclopedia_of_the_World&#39;s_Endangered_Languages_260-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Encyclopedia_of_the_World&#39;s_Endangered_Languages-260">&#91;256&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Tsakhur_language" title="Tsakhur language">Tsakhur</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-Encyclopedia_of_the_World&#39;s_Endangered_Languages_260-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Encyclopedia_of_the_World&#39;s_Endangered_Languages-260">&#91;256&#93;</a></sup> and <a href="/wiki/Udi_language" title="Udi language">Udi</a><sup id="cite_ref-Encyclopedia_of_the_World&#39;s_Endangered_Languages_260-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Encyclopedia_of_the_World&#39;s_Endangered_Languages-260">&#91;256&#93;</a></sup> are all spoken by small minorities. Some of these language communities are very small and their numbers are decreasing.<sup id="cite_ref-261" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-261">&#91;257&#93;</a></sup> Armenian was the majority language in Nagorno-Karabakh with around 76% in 1989.<sup id="cite_ref-262" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-262">&#91;258&#93;</a></sup> After the first Nagorno-Karabakh war, the population is almost exclusively Armenian at around 95%.<sup id="cite_ref-263" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-263">&#91;259&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Religion">Religion</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Religion_in_Azerbaijan" title="Religion in Azerbaijan">Religion in Azerbaijan</a> and <a href="/wiki/Irreligion_in_Azerbaijan" title="Irreligion in Azerbaijan">Irreligion in Azerbaijan</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Bibi_Heybat_Mosque_Baku_1.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7c/Bibi_Heybat_Mosque_Baku_1.jpg/220px-Bibi_Heybat_Mosque_Baku_1.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="164" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7c/Bibi_Heybat_Mosque_Baku_1.jpg/330px-Bibi_Heybat_Mosque_Baku_1.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7c/Bibi_Heybat_Mosque_Baku_1.jpg/440px-Bibi_Heybat_Mosque_Baku_1.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1200" data-file-height="894" /></a><figcaption>The <a href="/wiki/Bibi-Heybat_Mosque" title="Bibi-Heybat Mosque">Bibi-Heybat Mosque</a> in Baku. The mosque is built over the tomb of a descendant of <a href="/wiki/Muhammad" title="Muhammad">Muhammad</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Bibi_264-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Bibi-264">&#91;260&#93;</a></sup></figcaption></figure>
<p>Azerbaijan is considered the most secular Muslim-majority country.<sup id="cite_ref-265" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-265">&#91;261&#93;</a></sup> Around 97% of the population are Muslims.<sup id="cite_ref-266" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-266">&#91;262&#93;</a></sup> Around 55–85% of Muslims are estimated to be <a href="/wiki/Shia_Islam" title="Shia Islam">Shia</a>, while 15–45% of Muslims are <a href="/wiki/Sunni_Muslim" class="mw-redirect" title="Sunni Muslim">Sunnis</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Pres_4-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Pres-4">&#91;3&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-267" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-267">&#91;263&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-268" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-268">&#91;264&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-269" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-269">&#91;265&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-270" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-270">&#91;266&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-271" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-271">&#91;267&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-272" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-272">&#91;268&#93;</a></sup> Other faiths are practised by the country's various ethnic groups. Under article 48 of its <a href="/wiki/Constitution_of_Azerbaijan" title="Constitution of Azerbaijan">Constitution</a>, Azerbaijan is a <a href="/wiki/Secular_state" title="Secular state">secular state</a> and ensures religious freedom. In a 2006–2008 <a href="/wiki/Gallup_(company)" class="mw-redirect" title="Gallup (company)">Gallup</a> poll, only 21% of respondents from Azerbaijan stated that religion is an important part of their daily lives.<sup id="cite_ref-273" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-273">&#91;269&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Of the nation's religious minorities, the estimated 280,000 Christians (3.1%)<sup id="cite_ref-274" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-274">&#91;270&#93;</a></sup> are mostly <a href="/wiki/Russian_Orthodox_Church" title="Russian Orthodox Church">Russian</a> and <a href="/wiki/Georgian_Orthodox_Church" title="Georgian Orthodox Church">Georgian</a> <a href="/wiki/Eastern_Orthodox_Church" title="Eastern Orthodox Church">Orthodox</a> and <a href="/wiki/Armenian_Apostolic_Church" title="Armenian Apostolic Church">Armenian Apostolic</a> (almost all Armenians live in the break-away region of Nagorno-Karabakh).<sup id="cite_ref-cia_28-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cia-28">&#91;25&#93;</a></sup> In 2003, there were 250 <a href="/wiki/Roman_Catholics" class="mw-redirect" title="Roman Catholics">Roman Catholics</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-275" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-275">&#91;271&#93;</a></sup> Other Christian denominations as of 2002 include <a href="/wiki/Lutheranism" title="Lutheranism">Lutherans</a>, <a href="/wiki/Baptists" title="Baptists">Baptists</a> and <a href="/wiki/Molokan" title="Molokan">Molokans</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-AZR_276-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-AZR-276">&#91;272&#93;</a></sup> There is also a small <a href="/wiki/Protestant" class="mw-redirect" title="Protestant">Protestant</a> community.<sup id="cite_ref-277" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-277">&#91;273&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-278" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-278">&#91;274&#93;</a></sup> Azerbaijan also has an ancient <a href="/wiki/Jewish" class="mw-redirect" title="Jewish">Jewish</a> population with a <a href="/wiki/Mountain_Jews" title="Mountain Jews">2,000-year history</a>; Jewish organizations<sup class="noprint Inline-Template" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Words_to_watch#Unsupported_attributions" title="Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Words to watch"><span title="The material near this tag possibly uses too-vague attribution or weasel words. (June 2022)">who?</span></a></i>&#93;</sup> estimate that 12,000 Jews remain in Azerbaijan, which is home to the <a href="/wiki/Q%C4%B1rm%C4%B1z%C4%B1_Q%C9%99s%C9%99b%C9%99" title="Qırmızı Qəsəbə">only Jewish-majority town</a> outside of <a href="/wiki/Israel" title="Israel">Israel</a> and the <a href="/wiki/United_States" title="United States">United States</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-279" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-279">&#91;275&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-280" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-280">&#91;276&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-281" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-281">&#91;277&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-282" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-282">&#91;278&#93;</a></sup> Azerbaijan also is home to members of the <a href="/wiki/Bah%C3%A1%CA%BC%C3%AD_Faith" title="Baháʼí Faith">Baháʼí</a>, <a href="/wiki/International_Society_for_Krishna_Consciousness" title="International Society for Krishna Consciousness">Hare Krishna</a> and <a href="/wiki/Jehovah%27s_Witnesses" title="Jehovah&#39;s Witnesses">Jehovah's Witnesses</a> communities, as well as adherents of the other religious communities.<sup id="cite_ref-AZR_276-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-AZR-276">&#91;272&#93;</a></sup> Some religious communities have been <a href="/wiki/Freedom_of_religion_in_Azerbaijan#Restrictions_on_religious_freedom" title="Freedom of religion in Azerbaijan">unofficially restricted from religious freedom</a>. A <a href="/wiki/U.S._State_Department" class="mw-redirect" title="U.S. State Department">U.S. State Department</a> report on the matter mentions detention of members of certain Muslim and Christian groups, and many groups have difficulty registering with the agency who regulates religion, <a href="/wiki/The_State_Committee_on_Religious_Associations_of_the_Republic_of_Azerbaijan" title="The State Committee on Religious Associations of the Republic of Azerbaijan">The State Committee on Religious Associations of the Republic of Azerbaijan</a> (SCWRA).<sup id="cite_ref-283" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-283">&#91;279&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Education">Education</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Education_in_Azerbaijan" title="Education in Azerbaijan">Education in Azerbaijan</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Dunya1.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/de/Dunya1.jpg/220px-Dunya1.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/de/Dunya1.jpg/330px-Dunya1.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/de/Dunya1.jpg/440px-Dunya1.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3872" data-file-height="2592" /></a><figcaption>Classroom in <a href="/wiki/Khazar_University" title="Khazar University">Dunya School</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>A relatively high percentage of Azerbaijanis have obtained some form of higher education, most notably in scientific and technical subjects.<sup id="cite_ref-AZ_study_284-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-AZ_study-284">&#91;280&#93;</a></sup> In the Soviet era, literacy and average education levels rose dramatically from their very low starting point, despite two changes in the standard alphabet, from <a href="/wiki/Perso-Arabic_script" class="mw-redirect" title="Perso-Arabic script">Perso-Arabic script</a> to <a href="/wiki/Latin_script" title="Latin script">Latin</a> in the 1920s and from Roman to <a href="/wiki/Cyrillic" class="mw-redirect" title="Cyrillic">Cyrillic</a> in the 1930s. According to Soviet data, 100 percent of males and females (ages nine to forty-nine) were literate in 1970.<sup id="cite_ref-AZ_study_284-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-AZ_study-284">&#91;280&#93;</a></sup> According to the <a href="/wiki/United_Nations_Development_Program" class="mw-redirect" title="United Nations Development Program">United Nations Development Program</a> Report 2009, the literacy rate in Azerbaijan is 99.5 percent.<sup id="cite_ref-285" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-285">&#91;281&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Since independence, one of the first laws that Azerbaijan's Parliament passed to disassociate itself from the Soviet Union was to adopt a <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijani_alphabet" title="Azerbaijani alphabet">modified-Latin alphabet</a> to replace Cyrillic.<sup id="cite_ref-286" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-286">&#91;282&#93;</a></sup> Other than that the Azerbaijani system has undergone little structural change. Initial alterations have included the reestablishment of religious education (banned during the Soviet period) and curriculum changes that have reemphasized the use of the Azerbaijani language and have eliminated ideological content. In addition to elementary schools, the education institutions include thousands of preschools, general secondary schools, and <a href="/wiki/Vocational_schools" class="mw-redirect" title="Vocational schools">vocational schools</a>, including specialized secondary schools and technical schools. Education through the ninth grade is compulsory.<sup id="cite_ref-:02_287-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:02-287">&#91;283&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Culture">Culture</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Culture_of_Azerbaijan" title="Culture of Azerbaijan">Culture of Azerbaijan</a> and <a href="/wiki/Literature_of_Azerbaijan" class="mw-redirect" title="Literature of Azerbaijan">Literature of Azerbaijan</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/UNESCO_Intangible_Cultural_Heritage_List_in_Azerbaijan" title="UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage List in Azerbaijan">UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage List in Azerbaijan</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1096954695/mw-parser-output/.tmulti"><div class="thumb tmulti tright"><div class="thumbinner multiimageinner" style="width:418px;max-width:418px"><div class="trow"><div class="theader">The <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijani_rug" class="mw-redirect" title="Azerbaijani rug">Azerbaijani carpet</a> and <a title="Masterpieces of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity">Masterpiece of Intangible Heritage of Humanity</a></div></div><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:212px;max-width:212px"><div class="thumbimage"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:%C5%9E%C9%99kil-Bico_xal%C3%A7as%C4%B1_(1).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="An data-file-width="4752" data-file-height="3168" /></a></span></div></div></div></div></div>
<p>The culture of Azerbaijan has developed as a result of many influences; that's why Azerbaijanis are, in many ways, bi-cultural. Today, national traditions are well preserved in the country despite Western influences, including <a href="/wiki/Globalization" title="Globalization">globalized</a> consumer culture. Some of the main elements of the Azerbaijani culture are: music, literature, folk dances and art, cuisine, architecture, cinematography and <a href="/wiki/Novruz_in_Azerbaijan" title="Novruz in Azerbaijan">Novruz Bayram</a>. The latter is derived from the traditional celebration of the New Year in the ancient Iranian religion of <a href="/wiki/Zoroastrianism" title="Zoroastrianism">Zoroastrianism</a>. Novruz is a family holiday.<sup id="cite_ref-288" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-288">&#91;284&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The profile of Azerbaijan's population consists, as stated above, of Azerbaijanis, as well as other nationalities or ethnic groups, compactly living in various areas of the country. Azerbaijani national and traditional dresses are the <a href="/wiki/Chokha" title="Chokha">Chokha</a> and <a href="/wiki/Papakhi" class="mw-redirect" title="Papakhi">Papakhi</a>. There are radio broadcasts in Russian, <a href="/wiki/Georgian_language" title="Georgian language">Georgian</a>, <a href="/wiki/Kurdish_language" class="mw-redirect" title="Kurdish language">Kurdish</a>, <a href="/wiki/Lezgian_language" title="Lezgian language">Lezgian</a> and <a href="/wiki/Talysh_language" title="Talysh language">Talysh</a> languages, which are financed from the state budget.<sup id="cite_ref-MIN_256-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-MIN-256">&#91;252&#93;</a></sup> Some local radio stations in <a href="/wiki/Balak%C9%99n" title="Balakən">Balakan</a> and <a href="/wiki/Khachmaz_(city)" title="Khachmaz (city)">Khachmaz</a> organize broadcasts in <a href="/wiki/Avar_language" title="Avar language">Avar</a> and <a href="/wiki/Tat_language_(Caucasus)" title="Tat language (Caucasus)">Tat</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-MIN_256-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-MIN-256">&#91;252&#93;</a></sup> In Baku several newspapers are published in Russian, Kurdish (<i>Dengi Kurd</i>), Lezgian (<i>Samur</i>) and Talysh languages.<sup id="cite_ref-MIN_256-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-MIN-256">&#91;252&#93;</a></sup> Jewish society "Sokhnut" publishes the newspaper <i>Aziz</i>.<sup id="cite_ref-MIN_256-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-MIN-256">&#91;252&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Music_and_folk_dances">Music and folk dances</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Music_of_Azerbaijan" title="Music of Azerbaijan">Music of Azerbaijan</a> and <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijani_dances" title="Azerbaijani dances">Azerbaijani dances</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Uzeyir_Hajibeyov.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/18/Uzeyir_Hajibeyov.jpg/170px-Uzeyir_Hajibeyov.jpg" decoding="async" width="170" height="234" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/18/Uzeyir_Hajibeyov.jpg/255px-Uzeyir_Hajibeyov.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/18/Uzeyir_Hajibeyov.jpg/340px-Uzeyir_Hajibeyov.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2779" data-file-height="3822" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Uzeyir_Hajibeyov" title="Uzeyir Hajibeyov">Uzeyir Hajibeyov</a> merged traditional <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijani_music" class="mw-redirect" title="Azerbaijani music">Azerbaijani music</a> with Western styles in the early 20th century.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Music of Azerbaijan builds on <a href="/wiki/Folk_music" title="Folk music">folk traditions</a> that reach back nearly a thousand years.<sup id="cite_ref-289" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-289">&#91;285&#93;</a></sup> For centuries Azerbaijani music has evolved under the badge of <a href="/wiki/Monody" title="Monody">monody</a>, producing rhythmically diverse melodies.<sup id="cite_ref-EMD_290-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-EMD-290">&#91;286&#93;</a></sup> Azerbaijani music has a branchy <a href="/wiki/Musical_mode" class="mw-redirect" title="Musical mode">mode</a> system, where <a href="/wiki/Chromaticism" title="Chromaticism">chromatization</a> of <a href="/wiki/Major_and_minor" title="Major and minor">major and minor</a> <a href="/wiki/Musical_scale" class="mw-redirect" title="Musical scale">scales</a> is of great importance.<sup id="cite_ref-EMD_290-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-EMD-290">&#91;286&#93;</a></sup> Among national musical instruments there are 14 <a href="/wiki/String_instrument" title="String instrument">string instruments</a>, eight percussion instruments and six wind instruments.<sup id="cite_ref-291" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-291">&#91;287&#93;</a></sup> According to <i><a href="/wiki/The_New_Grove_Dictionary_of_Music_and_Musicians" title="The New Grove Dictionary of Music and Musicians">The Grove Dictionary of Music and Musicians</a></i>, "in terms of ethnicity, culture and religion the Azerbaijani are musically much closer to Iran than Turkey."<sup id="cite_ref-292" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-292">&#91;288&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Pht-Vugar_Ibadov_eurovision_(2).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/84/Pht-Vugar_Ibadov_eurovision_%282%29.jpg/220px-Pht-Vugar_Ibadov_eurovision_%282%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="159" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/84/Pht-Vugar_Ibadov_eurovision_%282%29.jpg/330px-Pht-Vugar_Ibadov_eurovision_%282%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/84/Pht-Vugar_Ibadov_eurovision_%282%29.jpg/440px-Pht-Vugar_Ibadov_eurovision_%282%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2682" data-file-height="1936" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Alim_Qasimov" title="Alim Qasimov">Alim Qasimov</a> performs <a href="/wiki/Mugham" title="Mugham">mugham</a> at <a href="/wiki/Eurovision_Song_Contest_2012" title="Eurovision Song Contest 2012">Eurovision Song Contest 2012</a>. The Azerbaijani Mugham was inscribed in 2008 as a <a href="/wiki/UNESCO" title="UNESCO">UNESCO</a> <a href="/wiki/Masterpieces_of_the_Oral_and_Intangible_Heritage_of_Humanity" title="Masterpieces of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity">Masterpiece of Intangible Heritage of Humanity</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<p><a href="/wiki/Mugham" title="Mugham">Mugham</a>, <a href="/wiki/Meykhana" title="Meykhana">meykhana</a> and <a href="/wiki/Art_of_Azerbaijani_ashiqs" class="mw-redirect" title="Art of Azerbaijani ashiqs">ashiq art</a> are among the many musical traditions of Azerbaijan. Mugham is usually a suite with poetry and instrumental interludes. When performing mugham, the singers have to transform their emotions into singing and music. In contrast to the mugham traditions of Central Asian countries, Azerbaijani mugham is more free-form and less rigid; it is often compared to the improvised field of <a href="/wiki/Jazz" title="Jazz">jazz</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-293" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-293">&#91;289&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/UNESCO" title="UNESCO">UNESCO</a> proclaimed the Azerbaijani mugham tradition a <a href="/wiki/Masterpieces_of_the_Oral_and_Intangible_Heritage_of_Humanity" title="Masterpieces of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity">Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity</a> on 7 November 2003. Meykhana is a kind of traditional Azerbaijani distinctive folk unaccompanied song, usually performed by several people improvising on a particular subject.<sup id="cite_ref-294" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-294">&#91;290&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Ashiq combines poetry, storytelling, dance, and vocal and instrumental music into a traditional performance art that stands as a symbol of Azerbaijani culture. It is a mystic troubadour or traveling bard who sings and plays the <a href="/wiki/Baglama" class="mw-redirect" title="Baglama">saz</a>. This tradition has its origin in the <a href="/wiki/Shamanistic" class="mw-redirect" title="Shamanistic">Shamanistic</a> beliefs of ancient <a href="/wiki/Turkic_peoples" title="Turkic peoples">Turkic peoples</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-European_University_Institute,_Florence,_Italy_295-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-European_University_Institute,_Florence,_Italy-295">&#91;291&#93;</a></sup> Ashiqs' songs are semi-improvised around common bases. Azerbaijan's ashiq art was included in the list of <a href="/wiki/Intangible_Cultural_Heritage" class="mw-redirect" title="Intangible Cultural Heritage">Intangible Cultural Heritage</a> by the UNESCO on 30 September 2009.<sup id="cite_ref-296" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-296">&#91;292&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Since the mid-1960s, Western-influenced <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijani_pop_music" title="Azerbaijani pop music">Azerbaijani pop music</a>, in its various forms, that has been growing in popularity in Azerbaijan, while genres such as <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijani_rock" title="Azerbaijani rock">rock</a> and <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijani_hip_hop" title="Azerbaijani hip hop">hip hop</a> are widely produced and enjoyed. Azerbaijani pop and <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijani_folk_music" title="Azerbaijani folk music">Azerbaijani folk music</a> arose with the international popularity of performers like <a href="/wiki/Alim_Qasimov" title="Alim Qasimov">Alim Qasimov</a>, <a href="/wiki/Rashid_Behbudov" title="Rashid Behbudov">Rashid Behbudov</a>, <a href="/wiki/Vagif_Mustafazadeh" title="Vagif Mustafazadeh">Vagif Mustafazadeh</a>, <a href="/wiki/Muslim_Magomayev_(musician)" title="Muslim Magomayev (musician)">Muslim Magomayev</a>, <a href="/wiki/Shovkat_Alakbarova" title="Shovkat Alakbarova">Shovkat Alakbarova</a> and <a href="/wiki/Rubaba_Muradova" title="Rubaba Muradova">Rubaba Muradova</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-297" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-297">&#91;293&#93;</a></sup> Azerbaijan is an enthusiastic participant in the Eurovision Song Contest. Azerbaijan made its debut appearance at the 2008 <a href="/wiki/Eurovision_Song_Contest_2008" title="Eurovision Song Contest 2008">Eurovision Song Contest</a>. The country's <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijan_in_the_Eurovision_Song_Contest_2009" title="Azerbaijan in the Eurovision Song Contest 2009">entry</a> gained third place in 2009 and fifth the following year.<sup id="cite_ref-298" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-298">&#91;294&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Eldar_%26_Nigar" class="mw-redirect" title="Eldar &amp; Nigar">Ell and Nikki</a> won the first place at the <a href="/wiki/Eurovision_Song_Contest_2011" title="Eurovision Song Contest 2011">Eurovision Song Contest 2011</a> with the song "<a href="/wiki/Running_Scared_(Eldar_%26_Nigar_song)" class="mw-redirect" title="Running Scared (Eldar &amp; Nigar song)">Running Scared</a>", entitling Azerbaijan to host the contest in <a href="/wiki/Eurovision_Song_Contest_2012" title="Eurovision Song Contest 2012">2012</a>, in Baku.<sup id="cite_ref-299" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-299">&#91;295&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-300" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-300">&#91;296&#93;</a></sup> They have qualified for every Grand Final up until the <a href="/wiki/Eurovision_Song_Contest_2018" title="Eurovision Song Contest 2018">2018 edition of the contest</a>, entering with <a href="/wiki/X_My_Heart_(song)" class="mw-redirect" title="X My Heart (song)">X My Heart</a> by singer <a href="/wiki/Aisel_(singer)" title="Aisel (singer)">Aisel</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-301" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-301">&#91;297&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>There are dozens of Azerbaijani <a href="/wiki/Folk_dance" title="Folk dance">folk dances</a>. They are performed at formal celebrations and the dancers wear national clothes like the <a href="/wiki/Chokha" title="Chokha">Chokha</a>, which is well-preserved within the national dances. Most dances have a very fast rhythm.<sup id="cite_ref-302" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-302">&#91;298&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Literature">Literature</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijani_literature" title="Azerbaijani literature">Azerbaijani literature</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Khurshidbanu_Natavan.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fd/Khurshidbanu_Natavan.jpg/180px-Khurshidbanu_Natavan.jpg" decoding="async" width="180" height="279" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fd/Khurshidbanu_Natavan.jpg/270px-Khurshidbanu_Natavan.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fd/Khurshidbanu_Natavan.jpg/360px-Khurshidbanu_Natavan.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2122" data-file-height="3289" /></a><figcaption>Painting of <a href="/wiki/Khurshidbanu_Natavan" title="Khurshidbanu Natavan">Khurshidbanu Natavan</a>, one of the most distinguished Azerbaijani poets. She was also the daughter of the last ruler of the <a href="/wiki/Karabakh_Khanate" title="Karabakh Khanate">Karabakh Khanate</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Among the medieval authors born within the territorial limits of modern Azerbaijani Republic was Persian poet and philosopher <a href="/wiki/Nizami_Ganjavi" title="Nizami Ganjavi">Nizami</a>, called Ganjavi after his place of birth, <a href="/wiki/Ganja,_Azerbaijan" title="Ganja, Azerbaijan">Ganja</a>, who was the author of the <a href="/wiki/Khamsa_of_Nizami" title="Khamsa of Nizami">Khamsa</a> ("The Quintuplet"), composed of five romantic poems, including "The Treasure of Mysteries", "Khosrow and Shīrīn", and "Leyli and Mejnūn".<sup id="cite_ref-303" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-303">&#91;299&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The earliest known figure in written Azerbaijani literature was <a href="/wiki/Izzeddin_Hasanoghlu" title="Izzeddin Hasanoghlu">Izzeddin Hasanoghlu</a>, who composed a <a href="/wiki/Diwan_(poetry)" title="Diwan (poetry)">divan</a> consisting of Persian and Azerbaijani <a href="/wiki/Ghazal" title="Ghazal">ghazals</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-beale_304-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-beale-304">&#91;300&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-caferoglu_305-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-caferoglu-305">&#91;301&#93;</a></sup> In Persian ghazals he used his pen-name, while his Azerbaijani ghazals were composed under his own name of Hasanoghlu.<sup id="cite_ref-beale_304-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-beale-304">&#91;300&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Classical literature in Azerbaijani was formed in the 14th century based on the various Early Middle Ages dialects of <a href="/wiki/Tabriz" title="Tabriz">Tabriz</a> and <a href="/wiki/Shirvan" title="Shirvan">Shirvan</a>. Among the poets of this period were <a href="/wiki/Kadi_Burhan_al-Din" title="Kadi Burhan al-Din">Gazi Burhanaddin</a>, <a href="/wiki/Jahan_Shah" title="Jahan Shah">Haqiqi</a> (pen-name of <a href="/wiki/Jahan_Shah" title="Jahan Shah">Jahan Shah Qara Qoyunlu</a>), and <a href="/wiki/Habibi_(poet)" title="Habibi (poet)">Habibi</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-tyrrell1_306-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-tyrrell1-306">&#91;302&#93;</a></sup> The end of the 14th century was also the period of starting literary activity of <a href="/wiki/Nesimi" class="mw-redirect" title="Nesimi">Imadaddin Nasimi</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-307" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-307">&#91;303&#93;</a></sup> one of the greatest Azerbaijani<sup id="cite_ref-308" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-308">&#91;304&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-burrill_309-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-burrill-309">&#91;305&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-310" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-310">&#91;306&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Hurufi" class="mw-redirect" title="Hurufi">Hurufi</a> <a href="/wiki/Mysticism" title="Mysticism">mystical</a> poets of the late 14th and early 15th centuries<sup id="cite_ref-nesimibritannica_311-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-nesimibritannica-311">&#91;307&#93;</a></sup> and one of the most prominent early divan masters in Turkic literary history,<sup id="cite_ref-nesimibritannica_311-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-nesimibritannica-311">&#91;307&#93;</a></sup> who also composed poetry in <a href="/wiki/Persian_language" title="Persian language">Persian</a><sup id="cite_ref-burrill_309-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-burrill-309">&#91;305&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-babinger_312-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-babinger-312">&#91;308&#93;</a></sup> and <a href="/wiki/Arabic_language" class="mw-redirect" title="Arabic language">Arabic</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-nesimibritannica_311-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-nesimibritannica-311">&#91;307&#93;</a></sup> The divan and ghazal styles were further developed by poets <a href="/wiki/Qasem-e_Anvar" class="mw-redirect" title="Qasem-e Anvar">Qasem-e Anvar</a>, <a href="/wiki/Fuz%C3%BBl%C3%AE" class="mw-redirect" title="Fuzûlî">Fuzuli</a> and <a href="/wiki/Khatai" class="mw-redirect" title="Khatai">Khatai</a> (pen-name of <a href="/wiki/Safavid_dynasty" title="Safavid dynasty">Safavid</a> <a href="/wiki/Shah_Ismail_I" class="mw-redirect" title="Shah Ismail I">Shah Ismail I</a>).
</p><p>The <i><a href="/wiki/Book_of_Dede_Korkut" title="Book of Dede Korkut">Book of Dede Korkut</a></i> consists of two manuscripts copied in the 16th century,<sup id="cite_ref-Meeker_313-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Meeker-313">&#91;309&#93;</a></sup> and was not written earlier than the 15th century.<sup id="cite_ref-Kafadar_314-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Kafadar-314">&#91;310&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-IranicaOguzKhan_315-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-IranicaOguzKhan-315">&#91;311&#93;</a></sup> It is a collection of 12 stories reflecting the oral tradition of Oghuz nomads.<sup id="cite_ref-IranicaOguzKhan_315-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-IranicaOguzKhan-315">&#91;311&#93;</a></sup> The 16th-century poet, Muhammed Fuzuli produced his timeless philosophical and lyrical <i>Qazals</i> in Arabic, Persian, and Azerbaijani. Benefiting immensely from the fine literary traditions of his environment, and building upon the legacy of his predecessors, Fuzuli was destined to become the leading literary figure of his society. His major works include <i>The Divan of Ghazals</i> and <i>The Qasidas</i>. In the same century, Azerbaijani literature further flourished with the development of <a href="/wiki/Ashik" title="Ashik">Ashik</a> (<a href="/wiki/Azerbaijani_language" title="Azerbaijani language">Azerbaijani</a>: <i lang="az">Aşıq</i>) poetic genre of bards. During the same period, under the pen-name of Khatāī (<a href="/wiki/Arabic_language" class="mw-redirect" title="Arabic language">Arabic</a>: <span lang="ar" dir="rtl">خطائی</span> for <i>sinner</i>) Shah Ismail I wrote about 1400 verses in Azerbaijani,<sup id="cite_ref-minorsky1_316-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-minorsky1-316">&#91;312&#93;</a></sup> which were later published as his <i>Divan</i>. A unique literary style known as <i>qoshma</i> (<a href="/wiki/Azerbaijani_language" title="Azerbaijani language">Azerbaijani</a>: <i lang="az">qoşma</i> for <i>improvisation</i>) was introduced in this period, and developed by Shah Ismail and later by his son and successor, Shah <a href="/wiki/Tahmasp_I" title="Tahmasp I">Tahmasp I</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Mino_317-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Mino-317">&#91;313&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In the span of the 17th and 18th centuries, Fuzuli's unique genres as well <a href="/wiki/Ashik" title="Ashik">Ashik</a> poetry were taken up by prominent poets and writers such as <a href="/wiki/Qovsi_of_Tabriz" class="mw-redirect" title="Qovsi of Tabriz">Qovsi of Tabriz</a>, <a href="/wiki/Abbas_II_of_Persia" title="Abbas II of Persia">Shah Abbas Sani</a>, <a href="/w/index.php?title=Agha_Mesih_Shirvani&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Agha Mesih Shirvani (page does not exist)">Agha Mesih Shirvani</a><sup class="noprint" style="font-style: normal;">&#160;&#91;<a href="https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%90%D0%B3%D0%B0_%D0%9C%D0%B0%D1%81%D0%B8%D1%85_%D0%A8%D0%B8%D1%80%D0%B2%D0%B0%D0%BD%D0%B8" class="extiw" title="ru:Ага Масих Ширвани">ru</a>&#93;</sup>, Nishat, <a href="/wiki/Molla_Vali_Vidadi" title="Molla Vali Vidadi">Molla Vali Vidadi</a>, <a href="/wiki/Molla_Panah_Vagif" title="Molla Panah Vagif">Molla Panah Vagif</a>, Amani, Zafar and others. Along with <a href="/wiki/Turkish_people" title="Turkish people">Turks</a>, <a href="/wiki/Turkmens" title="Turkmens">Turkmens</a> and <a href="/wiki/Uzbeks" title="Uzbeks">Uzbeks</a>, <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijanis" title="Azerbaijanis">Azerbaijanis</a> also celebrate the <a href="/wiki/Epic_of_Koroglu" class="mw-redirect" title="Epic of Koroglu">Epic of Koroglu</a> (from <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijani_language" title="Azerbaijani language">Azerbaijani</a>: <i lang="az">kor oğlu</i> for <i>blind man's son</i>), a legendary folk hero.<sup id="cite_ref-samuel_318-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-samuel-318">&#91;314&#93;</a></sup> Several documented versions of Koroglu epic remain at the Institute for Manuscripts of the <a href="/wiki/National_Academy_of_Sciences_of_Azerbaijan" class="mw-redirect" title="National Academy of Sciences of Azerbaijan">National Academy of Sciences of Azerbaijan</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-caferoglu_305-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-caferoglu-305">&#91;301&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Modern Azerbaijani literature in Azerbaijan is based on the Shirvani dialect mainly, while in Iran it is based on the Tabrizi one. The first newspaper in Azerbaijani, <i><a href="/wiki/Akinchi" title="Akinchi">Akinchi</a></i> was published in 1875.<sup id="cite_ref-319" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-319">&#91;315&#93;</a></sup> In the mid-19th century, it was taught in the schools of <a href="/wiki/Baku" title="Baku">Baku</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ganja_(city)" class="mw-redirect" title="Ganja (city)">Ganja</a>, <a href="/wiki/Shaki,_Azerbaijan" title="Shaki, Azerbaijan">Shaki</a>, <a href="/wiki/Tbilisi" title="Tbilisi">Tbilisi</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Yerevan" title="Yerevan">Yerevan</a>. Since 1845, it was also taught in the <a href="/wiki/University_of_Saint_Petersburg" class="mw-redirect" title="University of Saint Petersburg">University of Saint Petersburg</a> in Russia.<sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (October 2020)">citation needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Folk_art">Folk art</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijani_folk_art" class="mw-redirect" title="Azerbaijani folk art">Azerbaijani folk art</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Azerbaijan_tradition.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c4/Azerbaijan_tradition.jpg/170px-Azerbaijan_tradition.jpg" decoding="async" width="170" height="255" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c4/Azerbaijan_tradition.jpg/255px-Azerbaijan_tradition.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c4/Azerbaijan_tradition.jpg/340px-Azerbaijan_tradition.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1793" data-file-height="2689" /></a><figcaption>Traditional Azerbaijani clothing and musical instruments</figcaption></figure>
<p>Azerbaijanis have a rich and distinctive culture, a major part of which is <a href="/wiki/Decorative_art" class="mw-redirect" title="Decorative art">decorative</a> and <a href="/wiki/Applied_art" class="mw-redirect" title="Applied art">applied art</a>. This art form is represented by a wide range of handicrafts, such as chasing, jeweling, engraving in metal, carving in wood, stone, bone, carpet-making, lasing, pattern weaving and printing, and knitting and embroidery. Each of these types of decorative art, evidence of the endowments of the Azerbaijan nation, is very much in favor here. Many interesting facts pertaining to the development of arts and crafts in Azerbaijan were reported by numerous merchants, travelers, and diplomats who had visited these places at different times.<sup id="cite_ref-320" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-320">&#91;316&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijani_rug" class="mw-redirect" title="Azerbaijani rug">Azerbaijani carpet</a> is a traditional handmade textile of various sizes, with a dense texture and a pile or pile-less surface, whose patterns are characteristic of Azerbaijan's many carpet-making regions. In November 2010 the Azerbaijani carpet was proclaimed a <a href="/wiki/Masterpieces_of_the_Oral_and_Intangible_Heritage_of_Humanity" title="Masterpieces of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity">Masterpiece of Intangible Heritage</a> by <a href="/wiki/UNESCO" title="UNESCO">UNESCO</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-321" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-321">&#91;317&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-322" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-322">&#91;318&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Lahic_folk_art.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c0/Lahic_folk_art.png/220px-Lahic_folk_art.png" decoding="async" width="220" height="146" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c0/Lahic_folk_art.png/330px-Lahic_folk_art.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c0/Lahic_folk_art.png/440px-Lahic_folk_art.png 2x" data-file-width="4372" data-file-height="2906" /></a><figcaption>Handwork coppery in <a href="/wiki/Lah%C4%B1c,_Ismailli" title="Lahıc, Ismailli">Lahij</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>Azerbaijan has been since ancient times known as a center of a large variety of crafts. The archeological dig on the territory of Azerbaijan testifies to the well-developed agriculture, stock raising, metalworking, pottery, ceramics, and carpet-weaving that date as far back as to the 2nd millennium BC. Archeological sites in Dashbulaq, Hasansu, Zayamchai, and Tovuzchai uncovered from the BTC pipeline have revealed early Iron Age artifacts.<sup id="cite_ref-323" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-323">&#91;319&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Azerbaijani carpets can be categorized under several large groups and a multitude of subgroups. Scientific research of the Azerbaijani carpet is connected with the name of <a href="/wiki/Latif_Karimov" title="Latif Karimov">Latif Karimov</a>, a prominent scientist and artist. It was his classification that related the four large groups of carpets with the four geographical zones of Azerbaijan, Guba-Shirvan, Ganja-Kazakh, Karabakh and Tabriz.<sup id="cite_ref-324" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-324">&#91;320&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Cuisine">Cuisine</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijani_cuisine" title="Azerbaijani cuisine">Azerbaijani cuisine</a></div>
<figure class="mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Az%C9%99rbaycan_dolmas%C4%B1.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/86/Az%C9%99rbaycan_dolmas%C4%B1.jpg/240px-Az%C9%99rbaycan_dolmas%C4%B1.jpg" decoding="async" width="240" height="171" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/86/Az%C9%99rbaycan_dolmas%C4%B1.jpg/360px-Az%C9%99rbaycan_dolmas%C4%B1.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/86/Az%C9%99rbaycan_dolmas%C4%B1.jpg/480px-Az%C9%99rbaycan_dolmas%C4%B1.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1280" data-file-height="913" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Dolma" title="Dolma">Dolma</a>, a traditional Azerbaijani meal</figcaption></figure>
<p>The traditional cuisine is famous for an abundance of vegetables and greens used seasonally in the dishes. Fresh herbs, including mint, cilantro (coriander), dill, basil, parsley, tarragon, leeks, chives, thyme, marjoram, green onion, and watercress, are very popular and often accompany main dishes on the table. Climatic diversity and fertility of the land are reflected in the national dishes, which are based on fish from the <a href="/wiki/Caspian_Sea" title="Caspian Sea">Caspian Sea</a>, local meat (mainly mutton and beef), and an abundance of seasonal vegetables and greens. Saffron-rice <a href="/wiki/Plov" class="mw-redirect" title="Plov">plov</a> is the flagship food in Azerbaijan and <a href="/wiki/Black_tea" title="Black tea">black tea</a> is the national beverage.<sup id="cite_ref-325" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-325">&#91;321&#93;</a></sup> Azerbaijanis often use traditional <a href="/wiki/Armudu" title="Armudu">armudu</a> (pear-shaped) glass as they have very strong <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijani_tea_culture" title="Azerbaijani tea culture">tea culture</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-aze_326-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-aze-326">&#91;322&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-327" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-327">&#91;323&#93;</a></sup> Popular traditional dishes include <a href="/wiki/Bozbash" title="Bozbash">bozbash</a> (lamb soup that exists in several regional varieties with the addition of different vegetables), <a href="/wiki/Qutab" title="Qutab">qutab</a> (fried turnover with a filling of greens or minced meat) and <a href="/wiki/Dushbara" class="mw-redirect" title="Dushbara">dushbara</a> (sort of dumplings of dough filled with ground meat and flavor).
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Architecture">Architecture</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Architecture_of_Azerbaijan" title="Architecture of Azerbaijan">Architecture of Azerbaijan</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Momine_Hatoon_Mausoleum.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9e/Momine_Hatoon_Mausoleum.jpg/220px-Momine_Hatoon_Mausoleum.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9e/Momine_Hatoon_Mausoleum.jpg/330px-Momine_Hatoon_Mausoleum.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9e/Momine_Hatoon_Mausoleum.jpg/440px-Momine_Hatoon_Mausoleum.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1900" data-file-height="1270" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Momine_Khatun_Mausoleum" title="Momine Khatun Mausoleum">Momine Khatun Mausoleum</a> in <a href="/wiki/Nakhchivan_(city)" title="Nakhchivan (city)">Nakhchivan</a>, built in the 12th century</figcaption></figure>
<p>Azerbaijani architecture typically combines elements of <a href="/wiki/Eastern_world" title="Eastern world">East</a> and <a href="/wiki/Western_culture" title="Western culture">West</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-328" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-328">&#91;324&#93;</a></sup> Azerbaijani architecture has heavy influences from Persian architecture. Many ancient architectural treasures such as the <a href="/wiki/Maiden_Tower_(Baku)" title="Maiden Tower (Baku)">Maiden Tower</a> and <a href="/wiki/Palace_of_the_Shirvanshahs" title="Palace of the Shirvanshahs">Palace of the Shirvanshahs</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Baku" title="Baku">Walled City of Baku</a> survive in modern Azerbaijan. Entries submitted on the <a href="/wiki/UNESCO_World_Heritage" class="mw-redirect" title="UNESCO World Heritage">UNESCO World Heritage</a> tentative list include the <a href="/wiki/Ateshgah_of_Baku" title="Ateshgah of Baku">Ateshgah of Baku</a>, <a href="/wiki/Momine_Khatun_Mausoleum" title="Momine Khatun Mausoleum">Momine Khatun Mausoleum</a>, <a href="/wiki/Hirkan_National_Park" title="Hirkan National Park">Hirkan National Park</a>, <a href="/wiki/Binagadi_asphalt_lake" title="Binagadi asphalt lake">Binagadi asphalt lake</a>, <a href="/wiki/L%C3%B6kbatan_Mud_Volcano" title="Lökbatan Mud Volcano">Lökbatan Mud Volcano</a>, <a href="/wiki/Shusha_State_Historical_and_Architectural_Reserve" class="mw-redirect" title="Shusha State Historical and Architectural Reserve">Shusha State Historical and Architectural Reserve</a>, Baku Stage Mountain, Caspian Shore Defensive Constructions, Ordubad National Reserve and the <a href="/wiki/Palace_of_Shaki_Khans" title="Palace of Shaki Khans">Palace of Shaki Khans</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-329" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-329">&#91;325&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-330" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-330">&#91;326&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Among other architectural treasures are <a href="/wiki/Quadrangular_castle_(Mardakan)" class="mw-redirect" title="Quadrangular castle (Mardakan)">Quadrangular Castle</a> in <a href="/wiki/Mardakan" class="mw-redirect" title="Mardakan">Mardakan</a>, <a href="/wiki/Parigala" title="Parigala">Parigala</a> in <a href="/wiki/Yuxar%C4%B1_%C3%87ardaqlar" title="Yuxarı Çardaqlar">Yukhary Chardaglar</a>, a number of bridges spanning the Aras River, and several mausoleums. In the 19th and early 20th centuries, little monumental architecture was created, but distinctive residences were built in Baku and elsewhere. Among the most recent architectural monuments, the <a href="/wiki/Baku_Metro" title="Baku Metro">Baku subways</a> are noted for their lavish decor.<sup id="cite_ref-331" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-331">&#91;327&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The task for modern Azerbaijani architecture is diverse application of modern aesthetics, the search for an architect's own artistic style and inclusion of the existing historico-cultural environment. Major projects such as <a href="/wiki/Heydar_Aliyev_Cultural_Center" class="mw-redirect" title="Heydar Aliyev Cultural Center">Heydar Aliyev Cultural Center</a>, <a href="/wiki/Flame_Towers" title="Flame Towers">Flame Towers</a>, <a href="/wiki/Baku_Crystal_Hall" title="Baku Crystal Hall">Baku Crystal Hall</a>, <a href="/wiki/Baku_White_City" title="Baku White City">Baku White City</a> and <a href="/wiki/SOCAR_Tower" title="SOCAR Tower">SOCAR Tower</a> have transformed the country's skyline and promotes its contemporary identity.<sup id="cite_ref-332" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-332">&#91;328&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-333" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-333">&#91;329&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Visual_art">Visual art</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Visual_arts_of_Azerbaijan" class="mw-redirect" title="Visual arts of Azerbaijan">Visual arts of Azerbaijan</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Sheki_dvoretc_rospisi_az.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8b/Sheki_dvoretc_rospisi_az.jpg/400px-Sheki_dvoretc_rospisi_az.jpg" decoding="async" width="400" height="169" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8b/Sheki_dvoretc_rospisi_az.jpg/600px-Sheki_dvoretc_rospisi_az.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/8b/Sheki_dvoretc_rospisi_az.jpg 2x" data-file-width="800" data-file-height="337" /></a><figcaption>A <a href="/wiki/Miniature_(illuminated_manuscript)" title="Miniature (illuminated manuscript)">miniature painting</a> of a battle scene on the walls of the <a href="/wiki/Palace_of_Shaki_Khans" title="Palace of Shaki Khans">Palace of Shaki Khans</a>, 18th century, <a href="/wiki/Shaki,_Azerbaijan" title="Shaki, Azerbaijan">city of Shaki</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>The <a href="/wiki/Gamigaya_Petroglyphs" title="Gamigaya Petroglyphs">Gamigaya Petroglyphs</a>, which date back to the 1st to 4th millennium BC, are located in Azerbaijan's <a href="/wiki/Ordubad_District" title="Ordubad District">Ordubad District</a>. They consist of some 1500 dislodged and carved rock paintings with images of deer, goats, bulls, dogs, snakes, birds, fantastic beings, and people, carriages, and various symbols were found on basalt rocks.<sup id="cite_ref-334" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-334">&#91;330&#93;</a></sup> Norwegian <a href="/wiki/Ethnographer" class="mw-redirect" title="Ethnographer">ethnographer</a> and adventurer <a href="/wiki/Thor_Heyerdahl" title="Thor Heyerdahl">Thor Heyerdahl</a> was convinced that people from the area went to <a href="/wiki/Scandinavia" title="Scandinavia">Scandinavia</a> in about 100 AD, took their boat building skills with them, and transmuted them into the Viking boats in Northern Europe.<sup id="cite_ref-335" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-335">&#91;331&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-336" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-336">&#91;332&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Over the centuries, Azerbaijani art has gone through many stylistic changes. Azerbaijani painting is traditionally characterized by a warmth of colour and light, as exemplified in the works of <a href="/wiki/Azim_Azimzade" title="Azim Azimzade">Azim Azimzade</a> and <a href="/wiki/Bahruz_Kangarli" title="Bahruz Kangarli">Bahruz Kangarli</a>, and a preoccupation with religious figures and cultural motifs.<sup id="cite_ref-337" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-337">&#91;333&#93;</a></sup> Azerbaijani painting enjoyed preeminence in Caucasus for hundreds of years, from the <a href="/wiki/Romanesque_art" title="Romanesque art">Romanesque</a> and <a href="/wiki/Culture_of_the_Ottoman_Empire" title="Culture of the Ottoman Empire">Ottoman</a> periods, and through the <a href="/wiki/Socialist_realism" title="Socialist realism">Soviet</a> and <a href="/wiki/Baroque" title="Baroque">Baroque</a> periods, the latter two of which saw fruition in Azerbaijan. Other notable artists who fall within these periods include <a href="/wiki/Sattar_Bahlulzade" title="Sattar Bahlulzade">Sattar Bahlulzade</a>, <a href="/wiki/Togrul_Narimanbekov" title="Togrul Narimanbekov">Togrul Narimanbekov</a>, <a href="/wiki/Tahir_Salahov" title="Tahir Salahov">Tahir Salahov</a>, <a href="/wiki/Alakbar_Rezaguliyev" title="Alakbar Rezaguliyev">Alakbar Rezaguliyev</a>, <a href="/wiki/Mirza_Gadim_Iravani" class="mw-redirect" title="Mirza Gadim Iravani">Mirza Gadim Iravani</a>, <a href="/wiki/Mikayil_Abdullayev" title="Mikayil Abdullayev">Mikayil Abdullayev</a> and <a href="/wiki/Boyukagha_Mirzazade" title="Boyukagha Mirzazade">Boyukagha Mirzazade</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-338" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-338">&#91;334&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
