<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Cinema">Cinema</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Cinema_of_Azerbaijan" title="Cinema of Azerbaijan">Cinema of Azerbaijan</a>, <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijani_animation" class="mw-redirect" title="Azerbaijani animation">Azerbaijani animation</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Television_in_Azerbaijan" title="Television in Azerbaijan">Television in Azerbaijan</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Film_of_Azerbaijan_1916.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/Film_of_Azerbaijan_1916.jpg/220px-Film_of_Azerbaijan_1916.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="134" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/Film_of_Azerbaijan_1916.jpg/330px-Film_of_Azerbaijan_1916.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/Film_of_Azerbaijan_1916.jpg/440px-Film_of_Azerbaijan_1916.jpg 2x" data-file-width="800" data-file-height="489" /></a><figcaption>Scene from the Azerbaijani film <i><a href="/wiki/In_the_Kingdom_of_Oil_and_Millions" title="In the Kingdom of Oil and Millions">In the Kingdom of Oil and Millions</a></i>, 1916</figcaption></figure>
<p>The film industry in Azerbaijan dates back to 1898. Azerbaijan was among the first countries involved in <a href="/wiki/Cinematography" title="Cinematography">cinematography</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-mishon_339-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-mishon-339">&#91;335&#93;</a></sup> with the apparatus first showing up in <a href="/wiki/Baku" title="Baku">Baku</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-cinemainazerbaijan_340-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cinemainazerbaijan-340">&#91;336&#93;</a></sup> In 1919, during the <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijan_Democratic_Republic" title="Azerbaijan Democratic Republic">Azerbaijan Democratic Republic</a>, a documentary <i>The Celebration of the Anniversary of Azerbaijani Independence</i> was filmed on the first anniversary of Azerbaijan's independence from Russia, 27 May, and premiered in June 1919 at several theatres in Baku.<sup id="cite_ref-ocaz_341-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ocaz-341">&#91;337&#93;</a></sup> After the Soviet power was established in 1920, <a href="/wiki/Nariman_Narimanov" title="Nariman Narimanov">Nariman Narimanov</a>, Chairman of the Revolutionary Committee of Azerbaijan, signed a decree nationalizing Azerbaijan's cinema. This also influenced the creation of <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijani_animation" class="mw-redirect" title="Azerbaijani animation">Azerbaijani animation</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-ocaz_341-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ocaz-341">&#91;337&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In 1991, after Azerbaijan gained its independence from the Soviet Union, the first Baku International Film Festival East-West was held in Baku. In December 2000, the former President of Azerbaijan, Heydar Aliyev, signed a decree proclaiming 2 August to be the professional holiday of filmmakers of Azerbaijan. Today Azerbaijani filmmakers are again dealing with issues similar to those faced by cinematographers prior to the establishment of the Soviet Union in 1920. Once again, both choices of content and sponsorship of films are largely left up to the initiative of the filmmaker.<sup id="cite_ref-mishon_339-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-mishon-339">&#91;335&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Television">Television</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Media_of_Azerbaijan" class="mw-redirect" title="Media of Azerbaijan">Media of Azerbaijan</a> and <a href="/wiki/Media_freedom_in_Azerbaijan" title="Media freedom in Azerbaijan">Media freedom in Azerbaijan</a></div>
<p>There are three state-owned television channels: <a href="/wiki/AzTV" title="AzTV">AzTV</a>, <a href="/wiki/Idman_Azerbaijan_TV" title="Idman Azerbaijan TV">Idman TV</a> and <a href="/wiki/Medeniyyet_TV" title="Medeniyyet TV">Medeniyyet TV</a>. There is one public channel and 6 private channels: <a href="/wiki/%C4%B0ctimai_Television" title="İctimai Television">İctimai Television</a>, Space TV, <a href="/wiki/Lider_TV" title="Lider TV">Lider TV</a>, <a href="/wiki/Azad_Azerbaijan_TV" title="Azad Azerbaijan TV">Azad Azerbaijan TV</a>, <a href="/w/index.php?title=Xazar_TV&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Xazar TV (page does not exist)">Xazar TV</a><sup class="noprint" style="font-style: normal;">&#160;&#91;<a href="https://az.wikipedia.org/wiki/X%C9%99z%C9%99r_TV" class="extiw" title="az:Xəzər TV">az</a>&#93;</sup>, <a href="/w/index.php?title=Real_TV_(Azerbaijan)&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Real TV (Azerbaijan) (page does not exist)"> Real TV</a><sup class="noprint" style="font-style: normal;">&#160;&#91;<a href="https://az.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_TV_(Az%C9%99rbaycan)" class="extiw" title="az:Real TV (Azərbaycan)">az</a>&#93;</sup> and <a href="/wiki/Region_TV" class="mw-redirect" title="Region TV">ARB</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-342" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-342">&#91;338&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Human_rights">Human rights</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Human_rights_in_Azerbaijan" title="Human rights in Azerbaijan">Human rights in Azerbaijan</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Rashadat_Akhundov.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/13/Rashadat_Akhundov.jpg/220px-Rashadat_Akhundov.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="184" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/13/Rashadat_Akhundov.jpg/330px-Rashadat_Akhundov.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/13/Rashadat_Akhundov.jpg/440px-Rashadat_Akhundov.jpg 2x" data-file-width="960" data-file-height="801" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Rashadat_Akhundov" title="Rashadat Akhundov">Rashadat Akhundov</a>, the co-founder of <a href="/wiki/Nida_Civic_Movement" title="Nida Civic Movement">Nida Civic Movement</a>, was sentenced to 8 years of imprisonment on 6 May 2014.</figcaption></figure>
<p>The <a href="/wiki/Constitution_of_Azerbaijan" title="Constitution of Azerbaijan">Constitution of Azerbaijan</a> claims to guarantee freedom of speech, but this is denied in practice. After several years of decline in press and media freedom, in 2014, the media environment in Azerbaijan deteriorated rapidly under a governmental campaign to silence any opposition and criticism, even while the country led the Committee of Ministers of the <a href="/wiki/Council_of_Europe" title="Council of Europe">Council of Europe</a> (May–November 2014). Spurious legal charges and impunity in violence against journalists have remained the norm.<sup id="cite_ref-pace_343-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-pace-343">&#91;339&#93;</a></sup> All foreign broadcasts are banned in the country.<sup id="cite_ref-FH_344-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FH-344">&#91;340&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>According to the 2013 <a href="/wiki/Freedom_House" title="Freedom House">Freedom House</a> <a href="/wiki/Freedom_of_the_Press_(report)" title="Freedom of the Press (report)">Freedom of the Press report</a>, Azerbaijan's press freedom status is "not free", and Azerbaijan ranks 177th out of 196 countries.<sup id="cite_ref-345" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-345">&#91;341&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Christianity is officially recognized. All religious communities are required to register to be allowed to meet, under the risk of imprisonment. This registration is often denied. "Racial discrimination contributes to the country's lack of religious freedom, since many of the Christians are ethnic Armenian or Russian, rather than Azeri Muslim".<sup id="cite_ref-346" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-346">&#91;342&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-347" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-347">&#91;343&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Radio_Free_Europe/Radio_Liberty" title="Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty">Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty</a> and <a href="/wiki/Voice_of_America" title="Voice of America">Voice of America</a> are banned in Azerbaijan.<sup id="cite_ref-348" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-348">&#91;344&#93;</a></sup> Discrimination against <a href="/wiki/LGBT_rights_in_Azerbaijan" title="LGBT rights in Azerbaijan">LGBT people</a> in Azerbaijan is widespread.<sup id="cite_ref-349" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-349">&#91;345&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-350" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-350">&#91;346&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>During the last few years,<sup class="noprint Inline-Template" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Dates_and_numbers#Chronological_items" title="Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Dates and numbers"><span title="The time period mentioned near this tag is ambiguous. (December 2017)">when?</span></a></i>&#93;</sup> three journalists were killed and several prosecuted in trials described as unfair by international human rights organizations. Azerbaijan had the biggest number of journalists imprisoned in Europe in 2015, according to the <a href="/wiki/Committee_to_Protect_Journalists" title="Committee to Protect Journalists">Committee to Protect Journalists</a>, and is the 5th most censored country in the world, ahead of Iran and China.<sup id="cite_ref-351" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-351">&#91;347&#93;</a></sup> Some critical journalists have been <a href="/wiki/COVID-19_misinformation#Efforts_to_combat_misinformation" title="COVID-19 misinformation">arrested</a> for their coverage of the <a href="/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Azerbaijan" title="COVID-19 pandemic in Azerbaijan">COVID-19 pandemic in Azerbaijan</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-352" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-352">&#91;348&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-353" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-353">&#91;349&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>A report by an <a href="/wiki/Amnesty_International" title="Amnesty International">Amnesty International</a> researcher in October 2015 points to "...the severe deterioration of human rights in Azerbaijan over the past few years. Sadly Azerbaijan has been allowed to get away with unprecedented levels of repression and in the process almost wipe out its civil society."<sup id="cite_ref-354" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-354">&#91;350&#93;</a></sup> Amnesty's 2015/16 annual report<sup id="cite_ref-355" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-355">&#91;351&#93;</a></sup> on the country stated "... persecution of political dissent continued. Human rights organizations remained unable to resume their work. At least 18 prisoners of conscience remained in detention at the end of the year. Reprisals against independent journalists and activists persisted both in the country and abroad, while their family members also faced harassment and arrests. International human rights monitors were barred and expelled from the country. Reports of torture and other ill-treatment persisted."<sup id="cite_ref-356" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-356">&#91;352&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p><i><a href="/wiki/The_Guardian" title="The Guardian">The Guardian</a></i> reported in April 2017 that "Azerbaijan's ruling elite operated a secret $2.9bn (£2.2bn) scheme to pay prominent Europeans, buy luxury goods and launder money through a network of opaque British companies .... Leaked data shows that the Azerbaijani leadership, accused of serial human rights abuses, systemic corruption and rigging elections, made more than 16,000 covert payments from 2012 to 2014. Some of this money went to politicians and journalists, as part of an international lobbying operation to deflect criticism of Azerbaijan's president, Ilham Aliyev, and to promote a positive image of his oil-rich country." There was no suggestion that all recipients were aware of the source of the money as it arrived via a disguised route.<sup id="cite_ref-Gdn4917_357-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Gdn4917-357">&#91;353&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Sport">Sport</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Sport_in_Azerbaijan" title="Sport in Azerbaijan">Sport in Azerbaijan</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1096954695/mw-parser-output/.tmulti"><div class="thumb tmulti tright"><div class="thumbinner multiimageinner" style="width:344px;max-width:344px"><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:170px;max-width:170px"><div class="thumbimage"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:Mamedyarov,_Shamkir_2016.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f1/Mamedyarov%2C_Shamkir_2016.JPG/168px-Mamedyarov%2C_Shamkir_2016.JPG" decoding="async" width="168" height="253" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f1/Mamedyarov%2C_Shamkir_2016.JPG/252px-Mamedyarov%2C_Shamkir_2016.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/f1/Mamedyarov%2C_Shamkir_2016.JPG 2x" data-file-width="266" data-file-height="400" /></a></span></div><div class="thumbcaption text-align-center"><a href="/wiki/Shakhriyar_Mamedyarov" title="Shakhriyar Mamedyarov">Shakhriyar Mamedyarov</a> was the 2013 <a href="/wiki/World_Rapid_Chess_Championship" title="World Rapid Chess Championship">World Rapid Chess</a> and three-time <a href="/wiki/European_Team_Chess_Championship" title="European Team Chess Championship">European Team Chess</a> champion.</div></div><div class="tsingle" style="width:170px;max-width:170px"><div class="thumbimage"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:Teymur_R%C9%99c%C9%99bov.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/53/Teymur_R%C9%99c%C9%99bov.jpg/168px-Teymur_R%C9%99c%C9%99bov.jpg" decoding="async" width="168" height="253" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/53/Teymur_R%C9%99c%C9%99bov.jpg/252px-Teymur_R%C9%99c%C9%99bov.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/53/Teymur_R%C9%99c%C9%99bov.jpg 2x" data-file-width="266" data-file-height="400" /></a></span></div><div class="thumbcaption text-align-center"><a href="/wiki/Teimour_Radjabov" title="Teimour Radjabov">Teimour Radjabov</a> was the 2019 <a href="/wiki/Chess_World_Cup_2019" title="Chess World Cup 2019">World Cup</a> and three-time European Team Chess champion.</div></div></div></div></div>
<p>Freestyle wrestling has been traditionally regarded as Azerbaijan's <a href="/wiki/National_sport" title="National sport">national sport</a>, in which Azerbaijan won up to <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijan_at_the_Olympics" title="Azerbaijan at the Olympics">fourteen medals</a>, including four golds since joining the <a href="/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee" title="International Olympic Committee">International Olympic Committee</a>. Currently, the most popular sports include <a href="/wiki/Association_football" title="Association football">football</a> and wrestling.<sup id="cite_ref-358" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-358">&#91;354&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Football is the most popular sport in Azerbaijan, and the <a href="/wiki/Association_of_Football_Federations_of_Azerbaijan" title="Association of Football Federations of Azerbaijan">Association of Football Federations of Azerbaijan</a> with 9,122 registered players, is the largest sporting association in the country.<sup id="cite_ref-359" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-359">&#91;355&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-360" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-360">&#91;356&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijan_national_football_team" title="Azerbaijan national football team">national football team</a> of Azerbaijan demonstrates relatively low performance in the international arena compared to the nation football clubs. The most successful Azerbaijani football clubs are <a href="/wiki/Neft%C3%A7i_PFK" title="Neftçi PFK">Neftçi</a>, <a href="/wiki/Qaraba%C4%9F_FK" title="Qarabağ FK">Qarabağ</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Gabala_FK" class="mw-redirect" title="Gabala FK">Gabala</a>. In <a href="/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_UEFA_Europa_League" title="2012–13 UEFA Europa League">2012</a>, Neftchi Baku became the first Azerbaijani team to advance to the group stage of a European competition, beating <a href="/wiki/APOEL_F.C." class="mw-redirect" title="APOEL F.C.">APOEL</a> of Cyprus 4–2 on aggregate in the play-off round of the <a href="/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_UEFA_Europa_League" title="2012–13 UEFA Europa League">2012–13 UEFA Europa League</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-361" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-361">&#91;357&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-362" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-362">&#91;358&#93;</a></sup> In <a href="/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_UEFA_Europa_League" title="2014–15 UEFA Europa League">2014</a>, Qarabağ became the second Azerbaijani club advancing to the group stage of <a href="/wiki/UEFA_Europa_League" title="UEFA Europa League">UEFA Europa League</a>. In 2017, after beating <a href="/wiki/F.C._Copenhagen" title="F.C. Copenhagen">Copenhagen</a> 2–2 (<a href="/wiki/Away_goals_rule" title="Away goals rule">a</a>) in the play-off round of the <a href="/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_UEFA_Champions_League" title="2017–18 UEFA Champions League">UEFA Champions League</a>, Qarabağ became the first Azerbaijani club to reach the Group stage.<sup id="cite_ref-363" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-363">&#91;359&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Futsal" title="Futsal">Futsal</a> is another popular sport in Azerbaijan. The <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijan_national_futsal_team" title="Azerbaijan national futsal team">Azerbaijan national futsal team</a> reached fourth place in the <a href="/wiki/2010_UEFA_Futsal_Championship" title="2010 UEFA Futsal Championship">2010 UEFA Futsal Championship</a>, while domestic club <a href="/wiki/Araz_Nax%C3%A7ivan" title="Araz Naxçivan">Araz Naxçivan</a> clinched bronze medals at the <a href="/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_UEFA_Futsal_Cup" title="2009–10 UEFA Futsal Cup">2009–10 UEFA Futsal Cup</a> and <a href="/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Futsal_Cup" title="2013–14 UEFA Futsal Cup">2013–14 UEFA Futsal Cup</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-364" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-364">&#91;360&#93;</a></sup> Azerbaijan was the main sponsor of Spanish football club <a href="/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_de_Madrid" class="mw-redirect" title="Atlético de Madrid">Atlético de Madrid</a> during seasons 2013/2014 and 2014/2015, a partnership that the club described should 'promote the image of Azerbaijan in the world'.<sup id="cite_ref-365" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-365">&#91;361&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Azerbaijan is one of the traditional powerhouses of world chess,<sup id="cite_ref-366" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-366">&#91;362&#93;</a></sup> having hosted many international chess tournaments and competitions and became <a href="/wiki/European_Team_Chess_Championship" title="European Team Chess Championship">European Team Chess Championship</a> winners in 2009, 2013 and 2017.<sup id="cite_ref-367" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-367">&#91;363&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-368" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-368">&#91;364&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-369" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-369">&#91;365&#93;</a></sup> Notable chess players from the country's chess schools that have made a great impact on the game include <a href="/wiki/Teimour_Radjabov" title="Teimour Radjabov">Teimour Radjabov</a>, <a href="/wiki/Shahriyar_Mammadyarov" class="mw-redirect" title="Shahriyar Mammadyarov">Shahriyar Mammadyarov</a>, <a href="/wiki/Vladimir_Makogonov" title="Vladimir Makogonov">Vladimir Makogonov</a>, <a href="/wiki/Vugar_Gashimov" title="Vugar Gashimov">Vugar Gashimov</a> and former <a href="/wiki/World_Chess_Champion" class="mw-redirect" title="World Chess Champion">World Chess Champion</a> <a href="/wiki/Garry_Kasparov" title="Garry Kasparov">Garry Kasparov</a>. As of 2014<sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><a class="external text" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Azerbaijan&amp;action=edit">&#91;update&#93;</a></sup>, country's home of <a href="/wiki/Shamkir_Chess" title="Shamkir Chess">Shamkir Chess</a> a category 22 event and one of the highest rated tournaments of all time.<sup id="cite_ref-370" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-370">&#91;366&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Backgammon" title="Backgammon">Backgammon</a> also plays a major role in Azerbaijani culture.<sup id="cite_ref-371" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-371">&#91;367&#93;</a></sup> The game is very popular in Azerbaijan and is widely played among the local public.<sup id="cite_ref-372" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-372">&#91;368&#93;</a></sup> There are also different variations of backgammon developed and analyzed by Azerbaijani experts.<sup id="cite_ref-373" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-373">&#91;369&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Closing_ceremony_of_the_IV_Islamic_Solidarity_Games_15.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/39/Closing_ceremony_of_the_IV_Islamic_Solidarity_Games_15.jpg/240px-Closing_ceremony_of_the_IV_Islamic_Solidarity_Games_15.jpg" decoding="async" width="240" height="159" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/39/Closing_ceremony_of_the_IV_Islamic_Solidarity_Games_15.jpg/360px-Closing_ceremony_of_the_IV_Islamic_Solidarity_Games_15.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/39/Closing_ceremony_of_the_IV_Islamic_Solidarity_Games_15.jpg/480px-Closing_ceremony_of_the_IV_Islamic_Solidarity_Games_15.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2048" data-file-height="1361" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Baku_National_Stadium" class="mw-redirect" title="Baku National Stadium">Baku National Stadium</a> was used for the first <a href="/wiki/European_Games" title="European Games">European Games</a> in June 2015.</figcaption></figure>
<p><a href="/wiki/Azerbaijan_Women%27s_Volleyball_Super_League" title="Azerbaijan Women&#39;s Volleyball Super League">Azerbaijan Women's Volleyball Super League</a> is one of the strongest women leagues in the world. Its women's national team came fourth at the <a href="/wiki/2005_Women%27s_European_Volleyball_Championship" title="2005 Women&#39;s European Volleyball Championship">2005 European Championship</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-374" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-374">&#91;370&#93;</a></sup> Over the last years, clubs like <a href="/wiki/Rabita_Baku" class="mw-redirect" title="Rabita Baku">Rabita Baku</a> and <a href="/wiki/Azerrail_Baku" title="Azerrail Baku">Azerrail Baku</a> achieved great success at European cups.<sup id="cite_ref-375" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-375">&#91;371&#93;</a></sup> Azerbaijani volleyball players include likes of <a href="/wiki/Valeriya_Korotenko" class="mw-redirect" title="Valeriya Korotenko">Valeriya Korotenko</a>, <a href="/wiki/Oksana_Parkhomenko" class="mw-redirect" title="Oksana Parkhomenko">Oksana Parkhomenko</a>, <a href="/wiki/Inessa_Korkmaz" title="Inessa Korkmaz">Inessa Korkmaz</a>, <a href="/wiki/Natalya_Mammadova" title="Natalya Mammadova">Natalya Mammadova</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Alla_Hasanova" title="Alla Hasanova">Alla Hasanova</a>.
</p><p>Other Azerbaijani athletes are <a href="/wiki/Namig_Abdullayev" title="Namig Abdullayev">Namig Abdullayev</a>, <a href="/wiki/Toghrul_Asgarov" title="Toghrul Asgarov">Toghrul Asgarov</a>, <a href="/wiki/Rovshan_Bayramov" title="Rovshan Bayramov">Rovshan Bayramov</a>, <a href="/wiki/Sharif_Sharifov" title="Sharif Sharifov">Sharif Sharifov</a>, <a href="/wiki/Mariya_Stadnik" title="Mariya Stadnik">Mariya Stadnik</a> and <a href="/wiki/Farid_Mansurov" title="Farid Mansurov">Farid Mansurov</a> in <a href="/wiki/Amateur_wrestling" title="Amateur wrestling">wrestling</a>, <a href="/wiki/Nazim_Huseynov" title="Nazim Huseynov">Nazim Huseynov</a>, <a href="/wiki/Elnur_Mammadli" title="Elnur Mammadli">Elnur Mammadli</a>, <a href="/wiki/Elkhan_Mammadov_(judoka)" title="Elkhan Mammadov (judoka)">Elkhan Mammadov</a> and <a href="/wiki/Rustam_Orujov" title="Rustam Orujov">Rustam Orujov</a> in judo, <a href="/wiki/Rafael_Aghayev" title="Rafael Aghayev">Rafael Aghayev</a> in <a href="/wiki/Karate" title="Karate">karate</a>, <a href="/wiki/Magomedrasul_Majidov" title="Magomedrasul Majidov">Magomedrasul Majidov</a> and <a href="/wiki/Aghasi_Mammadov" title="Aghasi Mammadov">Aghasi Mammadov</a> in <a href="/wiki/Boxing" title="Boxing">boxing</a>, <a href="/wiki/Nizami_Pashayev" title="Nizami Pashayev">Nizami Pashayev</a> in <a href="/wiki/Olympic_weightlifting" title="Olympic weightlifting">Olympic weightlifting</a>, <a href="/wiki/Azad_Asgarov" title="Azad Asgarov">Azad Asgarov</a> in <a href="/wiki/Pankration" title="Pankration">pankration</a>, <a href="/wiki/Eduard_Mammadov" title="Eduard Mammadov">Eduard Mammadov</a> in kickboxing, and <a href="/wiki/K-1" title="K-1">K-1</a> fighter <a href="/wiki/Zabit_Samedov" title="Zabit Samedov">Zabit Samedov</a>.
</p><p>Azerbaijan has a <a href="/wiki/Baku_City_Circuit" title="Baku City Circuit">Formula One race-track</a>, made in June 2012,<sup id="cite_ref-376" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-376">&#91;372&#93;</a></sup> and the country hosted its first <a href="/wiki/2016_European_Grand_Prix" title="2016 European Grand Prix">Formula One Grand Prix</a> on 19 June 2016<sup id="cite_ref-377" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-377">&#91;373&#93;</a></sup> and the <a href="/wiki/Azerbaijan_Grand_Prix" title="Azerbaijan Grand Prix">Azerbaijan Grand Prix</a> in 2017, 2018, 2019, 2021 and 2022. Other annual sporting events held in the country are the <a href="/wiki/Baku_Cup" title="Baku Cup">Baku Cup</a> tennis tournament and the <a href="/wiki/Tour_d%27Azerba%C3%AFdjan" title="Tour d&#39;Azerbaïdjan">Tour d'Azerbaïdjan</a> cycling race.
</p><p>Azerbaijan hosted several major sport competitions since the late 2000s, including the <a href="/wiki/2013_F1_Powerboat_World_Championship_season" class="mw-redirect" title="2013 F1 Powerboat World Championship season">2013 F1 Powerboat World Championship</a>, <a href="/wiki/2012_FIFA_U-17_Women%27s_World_Cup" title="2012 FIFA U-17 Women&#39;s World Cup">2012 FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup</a>, <a href="/wiki/2011_AIBA_World_Boxing_Championships" title="2011 AIBA World Boxing Championships">2011 AIBA World Boxing Championships</a>, <a href="/wiki/2010_European_Wrestling_Championships" title="2010 European Wrestling Championships">2010 European Wrestling Championships</a>, <a href="/wiki/2009_Rhythmic_Gymnastics_European_Championships" title="2009 Rhythmic Gymnastics European Championships">2009 Rhythmic Gymnastics European Championships</a>, <a href="/wiki/European_Taekwondo_Championships" title="European Taekwondo Championships">2014 European Taekwondo Championships</a>, <a href="/wiki/2014_Rhythmic_Gymnastics_European_Championships" title="2014 Rhythmic Gymnastics European Championships">2014 Rhythmic Gymnastics European Championships</a>, and <a href="/wiki/42nd_Chess_Olympiad" title="42nd Chess Olympiad">2016 World Chess Olympiad</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-378" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-378">&#91;374&#93;</a></sup> On 8 December 2012, <a href="/wiki/Baku" title="Baku">Baku</a> was selected to host the <a href="/wiki/2015_European_Games" title="2015 European Games">2015 European Games</a>, the first to be held in the competition's history.<sup id="cite_ref-379" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-379">&#91;375&#93;</a></sup> Baku also hosted the fourth <a href="/wiki/Islamic_Solidarity_Games" title="Islamic Solidarity Games">Islamic Solidarity Games</a> in 2017<sup id="cite_ref-380" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-380">&#91;376&#93;</a></sup> and the <a href="/wiki/2019_European_Youth_Summer_Olympic_Festival" title="2019 European Youth Summer Olympic Festival">2019 European Youth Summer Olympic Festival</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-381" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-381">&#91;377&#93;</a></sup> and it is also one of the hosts of <a href="/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2020" title="UEFA Euro 2020">UEFA Euro 2020</a>, which because of <a href="/wiki/Covid-19" class="mw-redirect" title="Covid-19">Covid-19</a> is being held in 2021.<sup id="cite_ref-382" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-382">&#91;378&#93;</a></sup>
</p>

<li id="cite_note-LaPorte2016-8"><span class="mw-cite-backlink">^ <a href="#cite_ref-LaPorte2016_8-0"><sup><i><b>a</b></i></sup></a> <a href="#cite_ref-LaPorte2016_8-1"><sup><i><b>b</b></i></sup></a> <a href="#cite_ref-LaPorte2016_8-2"><sup><i><b>c</b></i></sup></a></span> <span class="reference-text"><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1133582631"><cite id="CITEREFLaPorte2016" class="citation book cs1">LaPorte, Jody (2016). "Semi-presidentialism in Azerbaijan". In <a href="/wiki/Robert_Elgie_(academic)" title="Robert Elgie (academic)">Elgie, Robert</a>; <a href="/wiki/Sophia_Moestrup" title="Sophia Moestrup">Moestrup, Sophia</a> (eds.). <i>Semi-Presidentialism in the Caucasus and Central Asia</i>. London: Palgrave Macmillan (published 15 May 2016). pp.&#160;91–117. <a href="/wiki/Doi_(identifier)" class="mw-redirect" title="Doi (identifier)">doi</a>:<a rel="nofollow" class="external text" href="https://doi.org/10.1057%2F978-1-137-38781-3_4">10.1057/978-1-137-38781-3_4</a>. <a href="/wiki/ISBN_(identifier)" class="mw-redirect" title="ISBN (identifier)">ISBN</a>&#160;<a href="/wiki/Special:BookSources/978-1-137-38780-6" title="Special:BookSources/978-1-137-38780-6"><bdi>978-1-137-38780-6</bdi></a>. <a href="/wiki/LCCN_(identifier)" class="mw-redirect" title="LCCN (identifier)">LCCN</a>&#160;<a rel="nofollow" class="external text" href="https://lccn.loc.gov/2016939393">2016939393</a>. <a href="/wiki/OCLC_(identifier)" class="mw-redirect" title="OCLC (identifier)">OCLC</a>&#160;<a rel="nofollow" class="external text" href="https://www.worldcat.org/oclc/6039791976">6039791976</a>. <q>LaPorte examines the dynamics of semi-presidentialism in Azerbaijan. Azerbaijan's regime is a curious hybrid, in which semi-presidential institutions operate in the larger context of authoritarianism. The author compares formal Constitutional provisions with the practice of politics in the country, suggesting that formal and informal sources of authority come together to enhance the effective powers of the presidency. In addition to the considerable formal powers laid out in the Constitution, Azerbaijan's president also benefits from the support of the ruling party and informal family and patronage networks. LaPorte concludes by discussing the theoretical implications of this symbiosis between formal and informal institutions in Azerbaijan's semi-presidential regime.</q></cite><span title="ctx_ver=Z39.88-2004&amp;rft_val_fmt=info%3Aofi%2Ffmt%3Akev%3Amtx%3Abook&amp;rft.genre=bookitem&amp;rft.atitle=Semi-presidentialism+in+Azerbaijan&amp;rft.btitle=Semi-Presidentialism+in+the+Caucasus+and+Central+Asia&amp;rft.place=London&amp;rft.pages=91-117&amp;rft.pub=Palgrave+Macmillan&amp;rft.date=2016&amp;rft_id=info%3Aoclcnum%2F6039791976&amp;rft_id=info%3Alccn%2F2016939393&amp;rft_id=info%3Adoi%2F10.1057%2F978-1-137-38781-3_4&amp;rft.isbn=978-1-137-38780-6&amp;rft.aulast=LaPorte&amp;rft.aufirst=Jody&amp;rfr_id=info%3Asid%2Fen.wikipedia.org%3AAzerbaijan" class="Z3988"></span></span>
</li>

<li id="cite_note-15"><span class="mw-cite-backlink"><b><a href="#cite_ref-15">^</a></b></span> <span class="reference-text">While often politically aligned with Europe, Azerbaijan is generally considered to be at least mostly in Southwest Asia geographically with its northern part bisected by the <a href="/wiki/Boundaries_between_the_continents_of_Earth" class="mw-redirect" title="Boundaries between the continents of Earth">standard Asia–Europe divide</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Greater_Caucasus" title="Greater Caucasus">Greater Caucasus</a>. The United Nations <a rel="nofollow" class="external text" href="http://unstats.un.org/unsd/methods/m49/m49regin.htm">classification of world regions</a> places Azerbaijan in Western Asia; the <a href="/wiki/CIA_World_Factbook" class="mw-redirect" title="CIA World Factbook">CIA World Factbook</a> places it mostly in Southwest Asia <a rel="nofollow" class="external autonumber" href="https://www.cia.gov/the-world-factbook/countries/azerbaijan/">[1]</a> and <a rel="nofollow" class="external text" href="http://www.m-w.com/dictionary/Azerbaijan"><i>Merriam-Webster's Collegiate Dictionary</i></a> places it in both; <a rel="nofollow" class="external text" href="http://www.nationalgeographic.com/xpeditions/atlas/index.html?Parent=asia&amp;Rootmap=azerba&amp;Mode=d&amp;SubMode=w">NationalGeographic.com</a>, and <a rel="nofollow" class="external text" href="https://www.britannica.com/EBchecked/topic/46781/Azerbaijan"><i>Encyclopædia Britannica</i></a> also place Georgia in Asia. Conversely, some sources place Azerbaijan in Europe such as <a rel="nofollow" class="external text" href="http://worldatlas.com/webimage/countrys/eu.htm">Worldatlas.com</a>.</span>
</li>

Unofficial Islamic groups sought to use aspects of Islam to mobilize the population and establish the foundations for a future political struggle.... Unlike Turkey, Azerbaijan does not have the powerful ideological legacy of secularism... the conflict with Armenia has bred frustration that is increasingly being answered by a combined Islamic and nationalist sentiment, especially among younger people... All major political forces are committed to secularism and are based, if anything, on a nationalist agenda.</q></cite><span title="ctx_ver=Z39.88-2004&amp;rft_val_fmt=info%3Aofi%2Ffmt%3Akev%3Amtx%3Abook&amp;rft.genre=book&amp;rft.btitle=Azerbaijan+Since+Independence&amp;rft.pages=165%2C+284&amp;rft.pub=M.E.+Sharpe&amp;rft.date=2010&amp;rft.aulast=Cornell&amp;rft.aufirst=Svante+E.&amp;rfr_id=info%3Asid%2Fen.wikipedia.org%3AAzerbaijan" class="Z3988"></span></span>

<li id="cite_note-Chaumont-38"><span class="mw-cite-backlink"><b><a href="#cite_ref-Chaumont_38-0">^</a></b></span> <span class="reference-text">Nevertheless, "despite being one of the chief vassals of Sasanian <i><a href="/wiki/Shahanshah" class="mw-redirect" title="Shahanshah">Shahanshah</a></i>, the Albanian king had only a semblance of authority, and the Sassanid <a href="/wiki/Marzban" title="Marzban">marzban</a> (military governor) held most civil, religious, and military authority.</span>

<li id="cite_note-Meeker-313"><span class="mw-cite-backlink"><b><a href="#cite_ref-Meeker_313-0">^</a></b></span> <span class="reference-text">Michael E. Meeker, "The Dede Korkut Ethic", International Journal of Middle East Studies, Vol. 24, No. 3 (Aug. 1992), 395–417. excerpt: The Book of Dede Korkut is an early record of oral Turkic folktales in Anatolia, and as such, one of the mythic charters of Turkish nationalist ideology. The oldest versions of the Book of Dede Korkut consist of two manuscripts copied in the 16th century. The twelve stories that are recorded in these manuscripts are believed to be derived from a cycle of stories and songs circulating among Turkic peoples living in northeastern Anatolia and northwestern Azerbaijan. According to Lewis (1974), an older substratum of these oral traditions dates to conflicts between the ancient Oghuz and their Turkish rivals in Central Asia (the Pecheneks and the Kipchaks), but this substratum has been clothed in references to the 14th-century campaigns of the Akkoyunlu Confederation of Turkic tribes against the Georgians, the Abkhaz, and the Greeks in Trebizond. Such stories and songs would have emerged no earlier than the beginning of the 13th century, and the written versions that have reached us would have been composed no later than the beginning of the 15th century. By this time, the Turkic peoples in question had been in touch with Islamic civilization for several centuries, had come to call themselves "Turcoman" rather than "Oghuz," had close associations with sedentary and urbanized societies, and were participating in Islamized regimes that included nomads, farmers, and townsmen. Some had abandoned their nomadic way of life altogether.</span>
</li>
<li id="cite_note-Kafadar-314"><span class="mw-cite-backlink"><b><a href="#cite_ref-Kafadar_314-0">^</a></b></span> <span class="reference-text">Cemal Kafadar(1995), "in Between Two Worlds: Construction of the Ottoman states", University of California Press, 1995. Excerpt: "It was not earlier than the fifteenth century. Based on the fact that the author is buttering up both the Akkoyunlu and Ottoman rulers, it has been suggested that the composition belongs to someone living in the undefined border region lands between the two states during the reign of Uzun Hassan (1466–78). G. Lewis, on the other hand, dates the composition "fairly early in the 15th century at least."</span>
</li>
